416	    /// `export_captions` — File ▸ Export Captions… (`CaptionExporter`, which
417	    /// owns the two containers and the round-trip rule). Writes one text
418	    /// track's clips out as SubRip (`.srt`) or WebVTT (`.vtt`). It edits
419	    /// nothing, so it answers through `jsonResult` rather than `editResult`
420	    /// and registers no undo step.
421	    ///
422	    /// **The track is never guessed**, and the rule is `CaptionExporter`'s
423	    /// rather than restated here: the default is the single track whose clips
424	    /// are all text, and with none or with more than one
425	    /// `CaptionExporter.resolveTrack` refuses and its `ExportError` LISTS the
426	    /// candidates by id, name and cue count. That is the posture
427	    /// `remove_media` takes for media still in use and `export` takes for an
428	    /// unknown size; picking the front-most candidate would write the wrong
429	    /// file and report success.
430	    ///
431	    /// The one thing this handler owns is the PATH, because a path is an
432	    /// argument rather than a caption question: the format is resolved first
433	    /// (an explicit `format` wins, else the path's own extension, else
434	    /// SubRip) so `captionDestinationURL` can replace a wrong extension rather
435	    /// than append to it — `talk.srt` asked for as `vtt` is `talk.vtt`, not
436	    /// `talk.srt.vtt`.
437	    func exportCaptions(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
438	        let document = try target(a)
439	        // The open container's, so the track this writes is the one
440	        // `get_project` is listing.
441	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
442	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
443	        let expanded = (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath
444	        let format = CaptionExporter.format(
445	            for: URL(fileURLWithPath: expanded), requested: try requestedFormat(a))
446	        let url = try Self.requireFolder(of: Self.captionDestinationURL(path, format: format))
447	
448	        // Read through `trackArg` rather than handed to the exporter raw, so
449	        // an id that names nothing is refused as "No track has id N" here
450	        // instead of arriving there as a track with no clips.
451	        var requestedTrack: UInt32?
452	        if a["track"] != nil, !(a["track"] is NSNull) {
453	            requestedTrack = try trackArg(a, "track", document).id
454	        }
455	        let outcome: (track: UInt32, format: CaptionExporter.Format, cues: [CaptionExporter.Cue])
456	        do {
457	            outcome = try CaptionExporter.export(
458	                from: snapshot, track: requestedTrack, to: url, format: format)
459	        } catch {
460	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
461	        }
462	        return try jsonResult([
463	            "ok": true,
464	            // The URL that was WRITTEN, never the argument: `destinationURL`
465	            // replaces a wrong extension, and every caller reports what
466	            // actually landed so the substitution is never silent.
467	            "path": url.path,
468	            "format": outcome.format.rawValue,
469	            "track": Int(outcome.track),
470	            "track_name": snapshot.track(outcome.track)?.name ?? "",
471	            "cues": outcome.cues.count,
472	            "project": summary(document),
473	        ])
474	    }

477	    /// trailing `srt` or `vtt` (`CaptionExporter.knownExtensions`) is
478	    /// replaced by the format's own, and any other extension is part of the
479	    /// name — `chart.png` is `chart.png.srt` — which is the save panel's rule
480	    /// (`CaptionExporter.renamed`), so the panel and the tool agree.
481	    static func captionDestinationURL(_ path: String, format: CaptionExporter.Format) -> URL {
482	        destinationURL(
483	            path, extension: format.rawValue, replacing: CaptionExporter.knownExtensions)
484	    }

486	    /// The `format` argument, refused BY NAME when it is not one of the two
487	    /// containers — nil when it is absent, which is what lets
488	    /// `CaptionExporter.format(for:requested:)` fall back to the path.
489	    private func requestedFormat(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> CaptionExporter.Format? {
490	        try enumArg(a, "format", CaptionExporter.Format.self, folding: true)
491	    }

495	/// `transcribe`'s CLOUD arm — road map 6 §5g. The engine argument, the three
496	/// arguments that only mean something with it, and the run itself.
497	///
498	/// It is a file of its own, and `AgentServer+Captions.swift` is otherwise the
499	/// code it was, for the reason §5g gives: the on-device path's refusals are a
500	/// story about an installed MODEL, the cloud path's are a story
501	/// about a CREDENTIAL and somebody else's service, and the two read as one
502	/// tangle when they are interleaved. What the two share — the scope, the
503	/// jobs, the frame, the cues, `CaptionLayout.place` and the result's shape —
504	/// stays over there and is reached exactly once from here, through this
505	/// method's two arguments and its answer.
506	///
507	/// **R6-2: `engine` is never remembered.** `TranscriptionEngine.defaultsKey`
508	/// is the SHEET's memory of what a person last chose, and this file does not
509	/// read it. An agent that wants its audio uploaded says so every time, which
510	/// is the only shape in which a call's meaning does not depend on what
511	/// somebody did in the UI an hour ago.
512	///
513	/// **R6-7: no `async`, and no queue of its own.** `CloudTranscriber.transcribe`
514	/// is the SYNCHRONOUS body, and this handler is already off main
515	/// (`AgentServer.offMainTools`), so the run happens on the server thread and
516	/// the wait IS the call — `transcribe`'s own argument for why it is in that
517	/// set, read across to an engine that waits on a socket instead of on a
518	/// recogniser.
519	///
520	/// **No credential is ever in an answer.** Not in a `ToolError`, not in a
521	/// `Problem`, not in the `note`: the only thing this file does with the
522	/// credential is hand it to `AssemblyAIClient.init`, which puts it in one
523	/// header and in no log line.
524	///
525	/// **R6-12, stated here because this is where it would be broken.** The KEY
526	/// and the REGION are a person's settings and no tool reads or writes
527	/// either: the key is R6-5's rule, and the region is a default a person sets
528	/// in the Settings window's Transcription pane, and it decides only WHERE a
529	/// transcript is made. So this file resolves both through
530	/// `AssemblyAIConfiguration` and offers neither as an argument, and
531	/// `cloudFields` names no region — every proof instance runs under
532	/// `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint`, where the region is not where the run spoke, so
533	/// the key could be proved only where it is false. The honest shape is the
534	/// one that has landed (#94): the run's client's HOST alone, under a key
535	/// named `endpoint` — a fact about where the requests went, never an
536	/// argument.
537	/// The vocabulary's rules are `TranscriptOptions.keyterms`, the one spelling
538	/// the sheet shares (c1-chrome moved them there verbatim).
539	extension AgentServer {
540	
541	    // MARK: - The engine argument
542	
543	    /// `engine`, refused BY NAME with both spellings when it is neither.
544	    ///
545	    /// Absent is `.apple`, and absent is the ONLY thing that makes it
546	    /// `.apple`: `UserDefaults` is not consulted here (R6-2). It is read
547	    /// through `stringArg`, so a number or an object is refused as a type
548	    /// error naming the key before the spelling is even looked at.
549	    func transcriptionEngine(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> TranscriptionEngine {
550	        guard let name = try stringArg(a, "engine") else { return .apple }
551	        guard let engine = TranscriptionEngine(rawValue: name) else {
552	            throw ToolError(
553	                message: "engine must be \"apple\" or \"assemblyai\" (got \"\(name)\").")
554	        }
555	        return engine
556	    }
557	
558	    /// The three arguments that only mean something to AssemblyAI, refused
559	    /// by name under `engine: "apple"`.
560	    ///
561	    /// `voice_confidence`-with-`mode: "level"`'s precedent (road map 4):
562	    /// an argument that cannot do anything is a MISTAKE, not a no-op, and
563	    /// dropping it quietly would let a caller believe a speaker-labelled
564	    /// transcript had been asked for and read the cues as if it had. The
565	    /// FIRST one present is the one named, in a fixed order, so the refusal
566	    /// is the same sentence for the same call every time.
567	    func refuseCloudOnlyArguments(_ a: [String: Any]) throws {
568	        for key in ["speakers", "vocabulary", "refresh"] {
569	            guard let value = a[key], !(value is NSNull) else { continue }
570	            throw ToolError(
571	                message: "\(key) only applies with engine \"assemblyai\". Pass engine: "
572	                    + "\"assemblyai\", or leave it out.")
573	        }
574	    }
575	
576	    // MARK: - The cloud run
577	
578	    /// The whole of the cloud arm: the three arguments, the vocabulary's
579	    /// rules, the credential, the endpoint, the run, and the result keys
580	    /// `Outcome` has no room for.
581	    ///
582	    /// **The refusal order is §5g's**, and every step of it is above the
583	    /// network on purpose. The caller's own mistakes are already answered by
584	    /// the time this is called (unknown clip, empty scope, misspelt engine);
585	    /// here it is the arguments' own types and values, then the CREDENTIAL,
586	    /// then the endpoint — and only then is a socket opened. A run that was
587	    /// going to be refused for a missing key must not first extract and
588	    /// upload half a gigabyte of audio to find that out.
589	    ///
590	    /// **The main thread is touched exactly once**, for the document's cache
591	    /// directory and its media records. Everything else the run needs is in
592	    /// the `Job`s by value, which is what lets the whole round trip happen
593	    /// off main with no document held.
594	    func cloudTranscription(
595	        _ a: [String: Any], document: ProjectDocument, jobs: [Transcriber.Job], frame: Ticks,
596	        pages: CaptionPages.Request, language: String?
597	    ) throws -> (outcome: Transcriber.Outcome, fields: [String: Any]) {
598	        let speakers = try boolArg(a, "speakers") ?? false
599	        let asked = try stringsArg(a, "vocabulary") ?? []
600	        let refresh = try boolArg(a, "refresh") ?? false
601	        let code = try Self.cloudLanguage(language)
602	        let vocabulary = TranscriptOptions.keyterms(asked)
603	
604	        var notes: [String] = []
605	        if asked.count > vocabulary.count, vocabulary.count == AssemblyAIClient.maxKeyterms {
606	            notes.append(
607	                "vocabulary was capped at \(AssemblyAIClient.maxKeyterms) terms (AssemblyAI's "
608	                    + "limit); \(asked.count) were given.")
609	        }
610	
611	        let credential = AssemblyAIConfiguration.credential(
612	            store: AssemblyAIConfiguration.store())
613	        var client: AssemblyAIClient?
614	        if let credential {
615	            do {
616	                let base = try AssemblyAIConfiguration.baseURL()
617	                client = AssemblyAIClient(base: base, credential: credential)
618	            } catch {
619	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
620	            }
621	        }
622	
623	        let context = try onMain { () -> (cache: URL, media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]) in
624	            guard let cache = document.cacheDirectory else {
625	                throw ToolError(
626	                    message: "This document has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it "
627	                        + "cannot be transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first.")
628	            }
629	            var records: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot] = [:]
630	            for entry in document.editedProject.snapshot.media { records[entry.id] = entry }
631	            return (cache, records)
632	        }
633	
634	        let options = TranscriptOptions(
635	            speechModels: TranscriptOptions.shippedModels, languageCode: code,
636	            speakerLabels: speakers, keytermsPrompt: vocabulary)
637	        let transcriber = CloudTranscriber(
638	            client: client,
639	            cacheDirectory: context.cache, media: context.media)
640	        let outcome: Transcriber.Outcome
641	        do {
642	            outcome = try transcriber.transcribe(
643	                jobs, options: options, refresh: refresh, frame: frame, pages: pages,
644	                cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken())
645	        } catch {
646	            // In band, message and all, exactly as the on-device arm does —
647	            // including "no speech was recognised", which is a true answer
648	            // about the audio rather than a transport problem.
649	            //
650	            // **A throw that came AFTER a bill says so.** `cloudFields` is
651	            // never reached on this path, so `uploaded` and `audio_seconds`
652	            // are not in the answer at all: a run whose only media held no
653	            // speech, or whose second media answered 401, told the caller
654	            // nothing about the money already spent (the reader review,
655	            // §10.13, R5·2). The facts go in the SENTENCE, which is the one
656	            // channel a throw has; the result KEYS are unchanged.
657	            throw ToolError(message: Self.cloudFailure(error, report: transcriber.report))
658	        }
659	        return (
660	            outcome,
661	            Self.cloudFields(transcriber.report, code: code, endpoint: client?.base.host, notes: notes)
662	        )
663	    }
664	
665	    /// What a FAILED run already cost, as a sentence to put after the
666	    /// failure's own — or nothing at all when it cost nothing.
667	    ///
668	    /// Only the media AssemblyAI actually answered for are counted:
669	    /// `report.uploaded` is written once per media that came back, so a media
670	    /// the run refused or could not reach is not in it.
671	    ///
672	    /// **It promises nothing about the cache.** It used to close with "their
673	    /// transcripts are cached in the project, so another run makes no request
674	    /// for them", which is false on the branch R1·3's fix created and issue
675	    /// #29 records: when `MediaTranscript.write` answers `false` the marker is
676	    /// (correctly) not written and NOTHING is cached, while the media is in
677	    /// `report.uploaded` all the same — so a caller who believed the sentence
678	    /// paid for the same media twice. The bill is what this method knows;
679	    /// what landed in the cache is not (the reader review's fix pass,
680	    /// §10.13).
681	    static func billed(_ report: CloudTranscriber.Report) -> String {
682	        guard !report.uploaded.isEmpty else { return "" }
683	        let seconds = report.billedSeconds
684	        let files = report.uploaded.count == 1 ? "1 media file" : "\(report.uploaded.count) media files"
685	        return " AssemblyAI had already been billed for \(files) (\(seconds) audio seconds) "
686	            + "before this failed."
687	    }
688	
689	    static func cloudFailure(_ error: any Error, report: CloudTranscriber.Report) -> String {
690	        let warnings = report.deletionWarnings { "media \($0)" }
691	            + report.cacheWarnings { "media \($0)" }
692	        return ([error.localizedDescription + billed(report)] + warnings)
693	            .joined(separator: "\n")
694	    }
695	
696	    /// `language` for the cloud engine: absent or `"auto"` is DETECTION,
697	    /// which is the wire's absent `language_code`; anything else is passed
698	    /// through trimmed.
699	    ///
700	    /// Nothing here checks the code against a table. C0's q5 measured that a
701	    /// code AssemblyAI does not support is a 400 at SUBMISSION in 0.24 s with
702	    /// its own sentence — so the cost of a wrong code is one wasted upload,
703	    /// and relaying the service's answer is better than carrying a second
704	    /// dated list of codes that can be wrong in the other direction. An
705	    /// EMPTY string is refused here, though: it is not a code and it is not
706	    /// "auto", and sending it would be asking for a language called "".
707	    private static func cloudLanguage(_ wanted: String?) throws -> String? {
708	        guard let wanted = wanted else { return nil }
709	        let trimmed = wanted.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
710	        guard !trimmed.isEmpty else {
711	            throw ToolError(
712	                message: "language cannot be empty. Pass a code like en, or \"auto\" to let "
713	                    + "AssemblyAI detect it, or leave it out.")
714	        }
715	        return trimmed.lowercased() == "auto" ? nil : trimmed
716	    }
717	
718	    /// The result keys the cloud engine adds — §5g's list, built from the
719	    /// run's own `Report` and from nothing else.
720	    ///
721	    /// `note` exists only when there is a part to put in it: R6-8's fallback
722	    /// ran, a vocabulary was cut, a remote delete is still owed, or a
723	    /// fetched transcript could not be kept for reuse. An empty
724	    /// note would be a key a caller has to read to learn nothing.
725	    ///
726	    /// `endpoint` is the HOST alone of the base URL the run's client spoke
727	    /// to (#94) — no scheme, port, path or userinfo, so no credential can
728	    /// ride in it (R6-5) — and it is absent when there was no client: a
729	    /// keyless run found no credential, built none, and sent nothing.
730	    static func cloudFields(
731	        _ report: CloudTranscriber.Report, code: String?, endpoint: String?, notes: [String]
732	    ) -> [String: Any] {
733	        var parts = notes
734	        let preferred = TranscriptOptions.shippedModels.first ?? "universal-3-5-pro"
735	        for row in report.uploaded {
736	            guard let model = row.speechModelUsed, model != preferred else { continue }
737	            parts.append(
738	                "AssemblyAI transcribed media \(row.media) with \(model), not \(preferred).")
739	        }
740	        parts.append(contentsOf: report.deletionWarnings { "media \($0)" })
741	        parts.append(contentsOf: report.cacheWarnings { "media \($0)" })
742	
743	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
744	            "engine": TranscriptionEngine.assemblyai.rawValue,
745	            "language": code ?? "auto",
746	            "uploaded": report.uploaded.map { Int($0.media) },
747	            "cached": report.cached.map { Int($0) },
748	            "audio_seconds": report.billedSeconds,
749	        ]
750	        let models: [[String: Any]] = report.uploaded.compactMap { row in
751	            guard let model = row.speechModelUsed else { return nil }
752	            return ["media": Int(row.media), "model": model]
753	        }
754	        if !models.isEmpty { fields["speech_model_used"] = models }
755	        // Only under detection: a code the caller NAMED comes back as itself
756	        // and reporting it as "detected" would be a false claim about how it
757	        // was arrived at (C0's q1 measured that `language_confidence` is
758	        // present only when the language was detected).
759	        if code == nil {
760	            let detected: [[String: Any]] = report.uploaded.compactMap { row in
761	                guard let answer = row.languageCode else { return nil }
762	                var out: [String: Any] = ["media": Int(row.media), "code": answer]
763	                if let confidence = row.languageConfidence { out["confidence"] = confidence }
764	                return out
765	            }
766	            if !detected.isEmpty { fields["language_detected"] = detected }
767	        }
768	        if let endpoint { fields["endpoint"] = endpoint }
769	        if !parts.isEmpty { fields["note"] = parts.joined(separator: " ") }
770	        return fields
771	    }
772	}

407	    /// The words the pager reads: trimmed, empties dropped, a word with

415	        var tokens: [(order: Int, word: CaptionCues.Word)] = []
416	        for word in words {
417	            for piece in word.text.split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace) {
418	                tokens.append((
419	                    tokens.count,

421	                        text: String(piece), start: word.start, end: word.end,
422	                        speaker: word.speaker)

426	        tokens.sort {
427	            $0.word.start == $1.word.start ? $0.order < $1.order : $0.word.start < $1.word.start

434	            let start = min(max(word.start + lead, lower), lastFrame)

508	    /// The pager over normalized tokens, each page within `span`.
509	    private static func page(
510	        _ tokens: [CaptionCues.Word], span: Range<Ticks>, request: Request, rules: Rules,
511	        clip: UInt32?
512	    ) -> [CaptionLayout.Cue] {

514	        guard !tokens.isEmpty else { return [] }
515	        let base = style.size(for: request.canvas)
516	        let budget = rules.widthBudget * Double(request.canvas.width)
517	        let pager = Pager(style: style, size: base, budget: budget, rules: rules)
518	
519	        var pages: [Page] = []
520	        var current: [CaptionCues.Word] = []
521	        func close(_ reason: Close) {
522	            guard !current.isEmpty else { return }
523	            pages.append(Page(words: current, close: reason))
524	            current = []
525	            pager.balance(&pages)
526	        }
527	
528	        for word in tokens {
529	            guard let previous = current.last, let first = current.first else {
530	                current = [word]
531	                continue
532	            }
533	            if word.speaker != previous.speaker || word.start - previous.end >= rules.breakGap

535	                || current.count >= (style.maxWords ?? Int.max)

538	                current = [word]
539	            } else if pager.lines(current + [word]) != nil {
540	                current.append(word)

543	                current = Array(current[...mark])
544	                close(.clause)
545	                current = rest + [word]
546	            } else {
547	                close(.width)
548	                current = [word]
549	            }
550	        }
551	        close(.end)

553	        var cues: [CaptionLayout.Cue] = []
554	        for (index, page) in pages.enumerated() {
555	            let first = page.words[0]
556	            let last = page.words[page.words.count - 1]
557	            let end: Ticks
558	            if index + 1 < pages.count {
559	                let next = pages[index + 1].words[0].start
560	                end = next - last.end < rules.breakGap ? next : min(next, last.end + rules.hold)

573	                CaptionLayout.Cue(
574	                    start: first.start, end: max(end, first.start), text: text,
575	                    tag: tag(at: first.start, clip: clip), words: page.words, size: size,
576	                    width: width))
577	        }
578	        return cues
579	    }

596	    /// The width arithmetic one run pages with: the style, its base size,
597	    /// the budget in pixels and the rules.
598	    private struct Pager {
599	        let style: CaptionStyle
600	        let size: Double
601	        let budget: Double
602	        let rules: Rules
603	
604	        static func endsSentence(_ text: String) -> Bool {
605	            guard let mark = text.last else { return false }
606	            return ".?!…".contains(mark)
607	        }
608	
609	        static func endsClause(_ text: String) -> Bool {
610	            guard let mark = text.last else { return false }
611	            return ",;:".contains(mark)
612	        }
613	
614	        func line(_ words: ArraySlice<CaptionCues.Word>) -> String {
615	            words.map(\.text).joined(separator: " ")
616	        }
617	
618	        /// The words laid greedily into at most `style.maxLines` lines, each
619	        /// within the budget — nil when they do not go. A line of one word
620	        /// wider than the budget is allowed only when it is the whole page:
621	        /// that is the lone word `shrink` answers for.
622	        func lines(_ words: [CaptionCues.Word]) -> [[CaptionCues.Word]]? {
623	            var out: [[CaptionCues.Word]] = []
624	            for word in words {
625	                if var last = out.last {
626	                    last.append(word)
627	                    if fits(line(last[...]), style: style, size: size, budget: budget) {
628	                        out[out.count - 1] = last
629	                        continue
630	                    }
631	                    guard out.count < style.maxLines else { return nil }
632	                }
633	                if words.count > 1, !fits(word.text, style: style, size: size, budget: budget) {
634	                    return nil
635	                }
636	                out.append([word])
637	            }
638	            return out
639	        }
640	
641	        /// The widest line of a page that lays, in pixels.
642	        func measure(_ words: [CaptionCues.Word]) -> Double {
643	            (lines(words) ?? [words]).map { width(line($0[...]), style, size) }.max() ?? 0
644	        }
645	
646	        /// Clause preference: a width break within `clauseWindow` words
647	        /// after a `,;:` moves back to the mark — when the page before it
648	        /// is at least `clauseMinimum` of the budget and what moves, with
649	        /// `word`, still lays. The index of the mark's word, or nil.
650	        func clauseMark(in page: [CaptionCues.Word], before word: CaptionCues.Word) -> Int? {
651	            let lowest = max(0, page.count - 1 - rules.clauseWindow)
652	            for mark in stride(from: page.count - 2, through: lowest, by: -1) {
653	                guard Self.endsClause(page[mark].text) else { continue }
654	                let head = Array(page[...mark])
655	                guard measure(head) >= rules.clauseMinimum * budget,
656	                      lines(Array(page[(mark + 1)...]) + [word]) != nil
657	                else { return nil }
658	                return mark
659	            }
660	            return nil
661	        }
662	
663	        /// The balance step, once per pair: when the page before the one
664	        /// just closed was closed by width alone, move its last word onto
665	        /// the new page if both still lay, no rule is broken, and their
666	        /// measured widths come closer. What stops a sentence ending on a
667	        /// one-word orphan while keeping every page within the budget.
668	        func balance(_ pages: inout [Page]) {
669	            guard pages.count >= 2 else { return }
670	            let before = pages[pages.count - 2]
671	            let after = pages[pages.count - 1]
672	            guard before.close == .width, before.words.count >= 2 else { return }
673	            let moved = before.words[before.words.count - 1]
674	            let kept = Array(before.words.dropLast())
675	            let grown = [moved] + after.words
676	            guard grown.count <= (style.maxWords ?? Int.max),
677	                  grown[grown.count - 1].end - moved.start <= rules.maxLength,
678	                  grown.allSatisfy({ $0.speaker == moved.speaker }),
679	                  lines(kept) != nil, lines(grown) != nil,
680	                  abs(measure(kept) - measure(grown))
681	                    < abs(measure(before.words) - measure(after.words))
682	            else { return }
683	            pages[pages.count - 2].words = kept
684	            pages[pages.count - 1].words = grown
685	        }
686	
687	        /// A lone word too wide for the budget: its size in 5 % steps of the
688	        /// base down to `shrinkFloor`, the first that fits — and when none
689	        /// does, the floor with `width = budget`, so CoreText wraps it.
690	        func shrink(_ text: String) -> (size: Double?, width: Double?) {
691	            let steps = Int(((1 - rules.shrinkFloor) / 0.05).rounded())
692	            for step in stride(from: 1, through: steps, by: 1) {
693	                let smaller = size * (1 - 0.05 * Double(step))
694	                if fits(text, style: style, size: smaller, budget: budget) {
695	                    return (smaller, nil)
696	                }
697	            }
698	            return (size * rules.shrinkFloor, budget)
699	        }
700	    }
701	}

4	/// SubRip, factored out of `CaptionImporter.swift` so the speech recogniser
5	/// (`Transcriber.swift`) lays its captions out exactly as an imported file's

7	/// `CaptionImporter`'s header doc is still where the reasoning for THAT lives.

10	/// the cue rules — at most two lines, at most 42 characters a line, at most
11	/// six seconds a cue, at least a frame between cues, and (road map 6 §5f) no
12	/// two speakers in one cue: five of them now — are "factored out

17	/// caption file people already import, and would break the 4b round trip

22	/// 1. snap each cue to the canvas frame grid (spec §5.1: the model never
23	///    stores a sub-frame time);

212	    /// A cue once the frame grid and its neighbours have had their say.
213	    private struct Placed {
214	        let tag: String
215	        /// The cue's index in the input, which is how a tie on `start` is
216	        /// broken. The importer used to break it on the SubRip line number;
217	        /// a parser emits its cues in file order and line numbers strictly
218	        /// increase, so the two orders are the same one — and this one also
219	        /// works for a producer whose tags are not numbers at all.
220	        let order: Int
221	        let start: Ticks
222	        var end: Ticks
223	        let text: String
224	        let words: [CaptionCues.Word]?
225	        let size: Double?
226	        let width: Double?
227	        let speaker: Speaker?
228	    }
229	
230	    /// Everything a caption run will do, computed against `project` and
231	    /// applied by nobody: the UI commits it through `ProjectDocument`, the
232	    /// agent through `AgentServer.editResult`.
233	    ///
234	    /// `existing` is whatever the producer already refused — a malformed SubRip
235	    /// block, an ineligible clip — and rides along so one report carries both
236	    /// halves.
237	    ///
238	    /// `track` places on an existing track; absent, the captions get a new
239	    /// front-most track of their own, which is the only placement that can
240	    /// never be refused by the overlap rule.
241	    ///
242	    /// `style` is the caption style (road map 8's W4a). `.subtitles` is the
243	    /// Caption preset and the code path this function always had, byte for
244	    /// byte for a cue with no speaker; a speaker's cue adds its palette
245	    /// `color` (`CaptionStyle.speakerColors`, spec §11 R6-22). A word
246	    /// style writes `style.pagePatch` per page — the props the pager measured,
247	    /// at the page's own size (a shrunk one or the style's), with its wrap
248	    /// width and its `words` in CLIP time — and puts the batch at the style's
249	    /// `y`, with the run's `looks` (W-15). `replacing` names caption tracks to remove
250	    /// WITH their clips in the same ops, first — `replaceableTracks` says
251	    /// which qualify — and the new track takes their place at the front.
252	    static func place(
253	        _ cues: [Cue], problems existing: [Problem] = [], in project: ReelProject,
254	        track: UInt32? = nil, trackBase: String = "Captions", style: CaptionStyle = .subtitles,
255	        looks: CaptionLooks = .none, replacing: [UInt32] = []
256	    ) throws -> Plan {
257	        let snapshot = project.snapshot
258	        let canvas = snapshot.canvas
259	        let frame = max(canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
260	        guard !cues.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.noCues(existing) }
261	
262	        // Snap, then give a cue that snapped to nothing its one frame back,
263	        // THEN resolve overlaps — in that order, so an overlap the minimum
264	        // length introduces is still one the overlap pass fixes.
265	        var placed = cues.enumerated().map { index, cue -> Placed in
266	            let start = ReelTime.snapToFrame(max(0, cue.start), fps: canvas.fps)
267	            let end = ReelTime.snapToFrame(cue.end, fps: canvas.fps)
268	            return Placed(
269	                tag: cue.tag, order: index, start: start, end: max(end, start + frame),
270	                text: cue.text, words: cue.words, size: cue.size, width: cue.width,
271	                speaker: cue.speaker)
272	        }
273	        placed.sort { $0.start == $1.start ? $0.order < $1.order : $0.start < $1.start }
274	
275	        // Captions are one track, so two cues on screen at once cannot both
276	        // be honoured: the later one wins its start and the earlier one is
277	        // cut back to it. That is also what the overlap rule (§6) would
278	        // otherwise refuse the placement over.
279	        var trimmed = 0
280	        for index in placed.indices.dropLast() where placed[index].end > placed[index + 1].start {
281	            placed[index].end = placed[index + 1].start
282	            trimmed += 1
283	        }
284	        var problems = existing
285	        for cue in placed where cue.end - cue.start < frame {
286	            problems.append(
287	                Problem(tag: cue.tag, reason: "starts less than a frame before the next caption"))
288	        }
289	        let kept = placed.filter { $0.end - $0.start >= frame }
290	        guard !kept.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.noCues(problems) }
291	
292	        // Before a single op: every op runs `Project::validate`, so a
293	        // transcript one clip too long would throw about clips, halfway
294	        // through, with the earlier ones already applied purely and thrown
295	        // away. The count is known here.
296	        let removed = Set(replacing)
297	        let room = Int(RC_MAX_CLIPS) - snapshot.clips.filter { !removed.contains($0.track) }.count
298	        guard kept.count <= room else {
299	            throw LayoutError.tooMany(cues: kept.count, room: max(0, room))
300	        }
301	
302	        // The replaced tracks go FIRST, clips and all: a removal mints no
303	        // id, so `next_id` below is still the new track's, and the new
304	        // track's index counts the stack as it will be once they are gone.
305	        var ops: [ReelOp] = replacing.map { .removeTrack(track: $0, withClips: true) }
306	        let destination: UInt32
307	        let name = trackName(in: snapshot, base: trackBase, excluding: replacing)
308	        if let track = track {
309	            destination = track
310	        } else {
311	            // A new id is `next_id` from BEFORE the op — the documented
312	            // contract of the one JSON entry point (§6), since an op returns
313	            // a project rather than an id. Index `tracks.count` is the front
314	            // of the stack, so captions draw over everything.
315	            destination = snapshot.nextId
316	            ops.append(.addTrack(index: snapshot.tracks.count - replacing.count, name: name))
317	        }
318	
319	        let preset = captionPreset
320	        let height = Double(canvas.height)
321	        let size = CGSize(width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height)
322	        var overTwoLines = 0
323	        if style.isWordStyle {
324	            let base = style.size(for: CGSize(width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height))
325	            for cue in kept {
326	                let words = cue.words.map { words in
327	                    words.map { TextWord(start: $0.start - cue.start, end: $0.end - cue.start) }
328	                }
329	                ops.append(
330	                    .addTextClip(
331	                        track: destination, at: cue.start, duration: cue.end - cue.start,
332	                        text: style.pagePatch(
333	                            content: cue.text, size: cue.size ?? base, width: cue.width,
334	                            words: words, looks: looks)))
335	            }
336	        } else {
337	            var base = TextPatch(
338	                font: preset.font, size: preset.size(on: size),
339	                align: preset.align, valign: "middle", backdrop: .some(preset.backdrop),
340	                width: .some(Double(canvas.width) * wrapFraction))
341	            if canvas.height > canvas.width {
342	                overTwoLines = kept.filter { measuresOverTwoLines($0.text, preset, on: size) }
343	                    .count
344	            }
345	            let colors = CaptionStyle.speakerColors(kept.map(\.speaker))
346	            for (cue, color) in zip(kept, colors) {
347	                base.content = cue.text
348	                base.color = color
349	                ops.append(
350	                    .addTextClip(
351	                        track: destination, at: cue.start, duration: cue.end - cue.start,
352	                        text: base))
353	            }
354	        }
355	
356	        // The preset's position is a `set_video` patch, and a patch needs
357	        // ids the ops have not minted yet — so the batch is applied PURELY
358	        // first and the ids read off the throwaway result. Applying the same
359	        // ops to the same handle mints the same ids, which is what makes
360	        // appending the patch to this very list correct
361	        // (`EditorViewController+AddClips.swift` does the same for one clip).
362	        //
363	        // The probe is kept rather than replaced by arithmetic on `next_id`:
364	        // ids ARE sequential when nothing is refused, and that is exactly the
365	        // invariant a refusal breaks — a caller-named track can refuse any
366	        // number of these placements, and then the patch would name clips
367	        // that do not exist.
368	        guard let probed = try project.applying(ops).project else { throw LayoutError.refused }
369	        let before = Set(snapshot.clips.map { $0.id })
370	        let created = probed.snapshot.clips.map { $0.id }.filter { !before.contains($0) }
371	        guard !created.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.refused }
372	        let at = preset.position(on: size)
373	        ops.append(
374	            .setVideo(
375	                clips: created,
376	                patch: style.isWordStyle
377	                    ? VideoPatch(x: 0, y: style.yFraction * height)
378	                    : VideoPatch(x: at.x, y: at.y, opacity: 1)))
379	
380	        return Plan(
381	            ops: ops, clips: created.count, cues: kept.count, trimmed: trimmed,
382	            problems: problems, trackName: track == nil ? name : nil, replaced: replacing,
383	            overTwoLines: overTwoLines)
384	    }

386	    /// Whether a Subtitles cue, as `place` writes it on `canvas` (the Caption preset, its
387	    /// wrap box), measures taller than the same props holding two lines (spec §11 VR-41).
388	    static func measuresOverTwoLines(
389	        _ content: String, _ preset: TextPreset, on canvas: CGSize
390	    ) -> Bool {
391	        func props(_ text: String) -> TextProps {
392	            TextProps(
393	                content: text, font: preset.font, size: preset.size(on: canvas),
394	                align: preset.align, valign: "middle", backdrop: preset.backdrop,
395	                width: Double(canvas.width) * wrapFraction)
396	        }
397	        return LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for: props(content)).height
398	            > LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for: props("X\nX")).height
399	    }
400	
401	    /// The tracks a restyle may replace (road map 8 §5e's three rules): a
402	    /// track named as this file names caption tracks ("Captions",
403	    /// "Captions N"), holding at least one clip and only text clips, each overlapping
404	    /// some job's `span` — so nothing outside the run's scope is removed.
405	    static func replaceableTracks(
406	        in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, jobs: [Transcriber.Job]
407	    ) -> [UInt32] {
408	        snapshot.tracks.compactMap { track -> UInt32? in
409	            guard isCaptionTrackName(track.name) else { return nil }
410	            guard snapshot.clips.contains(where: { $0.track == track.id }) else { return nil }
411	            for clip in snapshot.clips where clip.track == track.id {
412	                guard case .text = clip.source else { return nil }
413	                let end = clip.start + clip.duration
414	                guard jobs.contains(where: { $0.span.overlaps(clip.start ..< end) }) else {
415	                    return nil
416	                }
417	            }
418	            return track.id
419	        }
420	    }
421	
422	    /// A name this file gives a caption track: "Captions" or "Captions N".
423	    static func isCaptionTrackName(_ name: String) -> Bool {
424	        if name == "Captions" { return true }
425	        guard name.hasPrefix("Captions ") else { return false }
426	        let suffix = name.dropFirst("Captions ".count)
427	        return !suffix.isEmpty && suffix.allSatisfy { $0.isASCII && $0.isNumber }
428	    }
429	
430	    /// "Captions", then "Captions 2" — so two runs are tellable apart in the
431	    /// track header. `base` is the producer's word for what it made, and both
432	    /// producers say "Captions": a transcript and an imported file are the
433	    /// same thing on the timeline, and a second name would only make the
434	    /// numbering restart.
435	    /// A track in `excluding` is one this plan removes, so its name is free.
436	    static func trackName(
437	        in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, base: String = "Captions", excluding: [UInt32] = []
438	    ) -> String {
439	        let taken = Set(snapshot.tracks.filter { !excluding.contains($0.id) }.map { $0.name })
440	        var name = base
441	        var suffix = 2
442	        while taken.contains(name) {
443	            name = "\(base) \(suffix)"
444	            suffix += 1
445	        }
446	        return name
447	    }
448	}

452	/// Word caption pages re-paged from their own words on the current canvas (spec §11 VR-40):
453	/// what File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas and `relay_captions` do (VR-45), and step (6) of
454	/// Make Vertical (`VerticalVersion+Plan.swift`). W-7 and W-10 stand: `CaptionPages.repage` is
455	/// the measuring pager with lead 0 and `CaptionLayout.place` the one writer, so a re-laid page
456	/// is built exactly as a generated one is — from the words the pages hold, so every correction
457	/// is kept (the owner's answer, 2026-11-01).
458	///
459	/// `place(replacing:)` removes each replaced track with its clips first, so a track is
460	/// replaced only when every page on it is recognised: a track holding a page with no timings,
461	/// or in a style Frame Job does not make, is KEPT and named with its reason. Names no `rc_*`.
462	enum CaptionRelayout {
463	    /// The undo step's name (VR-45).
464	    static let actionName = "Re-lay Captions"
465	
466	    /// A caption track whose pages are all in one recognised style.
467	    struct Track: Equatable {
468	        let track: UInt32
469	        let name: String
470	        let style: CaptionStyle
471	        let looks: CaptionLooks
472	    }
473	
474	    /// A caption track left as placed, and why.
475	    struct Kept: Equatable {
476	        let track: UInt32
477	        let name: String
478	        let reason: String
479	    }
480	
481	    /// A track re-laid: the new track's id, the old one's, its name, style and page count.
482	    struct Relaid: Equatable {
483	        let track: UInt32
484	        let replaced: UInt32
485	        let name: String
486	        let style: CaptionStyle
487	        let pages: Int
488	    }
489	
490	    /// What the survey found, each list in stack order, back first.
491	    struct Survey: Equatable {
492	        let recognised: [Track]
493	        let kept: [Kept]
494	    }
495	
496	    struct Outcome: Equatable {
497	        var relaid: [Relaid]
498	        var kept: [Kept]
499	    }
500	
501	    /// VR-40 (a): the caption tracks of one container — named as `CaptionLayout` names them,
502	    /// holding at least one clip and only text clips — each recognised or kept with the first
503	    /// reason that applies.
504	    static func survey(_ snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Survey {
505	        var recognised: [Track] = []
506	        var kept: [Kept] = []
507	        for track in snapshot.tracks where CaptionLayout.isCaptionTrackName(track.name) {
508	            let clips = snapshot.clips(onTrack: track.id)
509	            guard !clips.isEmpty, clips.allSatisfy(isText) else { continue }
510	            func keep(_ reason: String) {
511	                kept.append(Kept(track: track.id, name: track.name, reason: reason))
512	            }
513	            if track.matte != .none {
514	                keep("it is a matte track")
515	                continue
516	            }
517	            let timed = clips.map { Self.words(of: $0) }
518	            if timed.contains(where: { $0 == nil }) {
519	                keep("it holds a page with no word timings")
520	                continue
521	            }
522	            if timed.contains(where: { $0?.isEmpty ?? true }) {
523	                keep("it holds a page none of whose words starts inside it")
524	                continue
525	            }
526	            let styles = clips.map { clip in clip.text.flatMap(recognise) }
527	            if styles.contains(where: { $0 == nil }) {
528	                keep("it holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make")
529	                continue
530	            }
531	            guard let first = styles[0],
532	                styles.allSatisfy({ $0?.style == first.style && $0?.looks == first.looks })
533	            else {
534	                keep("its pages are in more than one style")
535	                continue
536	            }
537	            recognised.append(
538	                Track(track: track.id, name: track.name, style: first.style, looks: first.looks))
539	        }
540	        return Survey(recognised: recognised, kept: kept)
541	    }
542	
543	    private static func isText(_ clip: ClipSnapshot) -> Bool {
544	        if case .text = clip.source { return true }
545	        return false
546	    }
547	
548	    /// VR-40 (b): the word style and looks a page was made in — its font the style's and its
549	    /// `word_style` the style's with those looks — or nil. Subtitles is never a match.
550	    static func recognise(_ text: TextProps) -> (style: CaptionStyle, looks: CaptionLooks)? {
551	        for style in CaptionStyle.allCases where style.isWordStyle && text.font == style.font {
552	            for bits in 0 ..< 8 {
553	                let looks = CaptionLooks(
554	                    slide: bits & 1 != 0, fill: bits & 2 != 0, dim: bits & 4 != 0)
555	                guard looks == looks.live(for: style) else { continue }
556	                if text.wordStyle == style.wordStyle(looks) { return (style, looks) }
557	            }
558	        }
559	        return nil
560	    }
561	
562	    /// VR-40 (c): a page's timed words in TIMELINE ticks, one per whitespace token of
563	    /// `content`, speaker nil — only those whose start lies inside the clip (a split's or a
564	    /// trim's half holds the words of the part it lost). Nil for a clip with no text, no
565	    /// words or a count that differs from the tokens; empty when none starts inside.
566	    static func words(of clip: ClipSnapshot) -> [CaptionCues.Word]? {
567	        guard let text = clip.text, !text.words.isEmpty else { return nil }
568	        let tokens = text.content.split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace)
569	        guard tokens.count == text.words.count else { return nil }
570	        let inside = clip.start ..< clip.start + clip.duration
571	        return zip(tokens, text.words).compactMap { token, word in
572	            let start = clip.start + word.start
573	            guard inside.contains(start) else { return nil }
574	            return CaptionCues.Word(
575	                text: String(token), start: start, end: clip.start + word.end, speaker: nil)
576	        }
577	    }

579	    /// VR-40 (e): each track re-paged on the trial's canvas, back to front, as one batch per
580	    /// track tried op by op on a scratch copy; a `LayoutError` or a refusal keeps the track
581	    /// and applies nothing of it. Then the new track back at the old one's index, hidden and
582	    /// locked as it was. Throws only the core's invalid input.
583	    static func relay(_ tracks: [Track], on trial: inout SwitchAngle.Trial) throws -> Outcome {
584	        var outcome = Outcome(relaid: [], kept: [])
585	        for track in tracks {
586	            let before = trial.project.snapshot
587	            guard let index = before.tracks.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == track.track }) else {
588	                continue
589	            }
590	            let old = before.tracks[index]
591	            let canvas = CGSize(width: before.canvas.width, height: before.canvas.height)
592	            let frame = max(before.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
593	            let request = CaptionPages.Request(style: track.style, canvas: canvas)
594	            var cues: [CaptionLayout.Cue] = []
595	            for clip in before.clips(onTrack: track.track).sorted(by: { $0.start < $1.start }) {
596	                cues += CaptionPages.repage(
597	                    words(of: clip) ?? [], span: clip.start ..< clip.start + clip.duration,
598	                    frame: frame, request: request, clip: clip.id)
599	            }
600	            func keep(_ reason: String) {
601	                outcome.kept.append(Kept(track: track.track, name: track.name, reason: reason))
602	            }
603	            let plan: CaptionLayout.Plan
604	            do {
605	                plan = try CaptionLayout.place(
606	                    cues, in: trial.project, trackBase: track.name, style: track.style,
607	                    looks: track.looks, replacing: [track.track])
608	            } catch let error as CaptionLayout.LayoutError {
609	                keep(error.errorDescription ?? "the captions could not be placed")
610	                continue
611	            }
612	            var scratch = trial
613	            var refused: String?
614	            for op in plan.ops {
615	                if let why = try scratch.require(op) {
616	                    refused = why
617	                    break
618	                }
619	            }
620	            if let refused {
621	                keep(refused)
622	                continue
623	            }
624	            let known = Set(before.tracks.map(\.id))
625	            guard
626	                let made = scratch.project.snapshot.tracks.first(where: {
627	                    !known.contains($0.id)
628	                })
629	            else {
630	                keep("no caption track was made")
631	                continue
632	            }
633	            var follow: [ReelOp] = [.moveTrack(track: made.id, index: index)]
634	            if old.hidden { follow.append(.setTrack(track: made.id, hidden: true)) }
635	            if old.locked { follow.append(.setTrack(track: made.id, locked: true)) }
636	            for op in follow {
637	                if let why = try scratch.require(op) {
638	                    refused = why
639	                    break
640	                }
641	            }
642	            if let refused {
643	                keep(refused)
644	                continue
645	            }
646	            trial = scratch
647	            outcome.relaid.append(
648	                Relaid(
649	                    track: made.id, replaced: track.track, name: made.name, style: track.style,
650	                    pages: plan.clips))
651	        }
652	        return outcome
653	    }

655	    /// VR-45: the survey and the re-lay of one container's handle (the editor's
656	    /// `editedProject`); the outcome's kept tracks are the survey's, then the re-lay's.
657	    static func plan(_ project: ReelProject) throws -> (ops: [ReelOp], outcome: Outcome) {
658	        let found = survey(project.snapshot)
659	        var trial = SwitchAngle.Trial(project: project)
660	        var outcome = try relay(found.recognised, on: &trial)
661	        outcome.kept = found.kept + outcome.kept
662	        return (trial.ops, outcome)
663	    }

508	    /// The pager over normalized tokens, each page within `span`.
509	    private static func page(
510	        _ tokens: [CaptionCues.Word], span: Range<Ticks>, request: Request, rules: Rules,
511	        clip: UInt32?

514	        guard !tokens.isEmpty else { return [] }

516	        let budget = rules.widthBudget * Double(request.canvas.width)
517	        let pager = Pager(style: style, size: base, budget: budget, rules: rules)
518	
519	        var pages: [Page] = []
520	        var current: [CaptionCues.Word] = []
521	        func close(_ reason: Close) {
522	            guard !current.isEmpty else { return }
523	            pages.append(Page(words: current, close: reason))
524	            current = []
525	            pager.balance(&pages)
526	        }
527	
528	        for word in tokens {
529	            guard let previous = current.last, let first = current.first else {
530	                current = [word]
531	                continue
532	            }
533	            if word.speaker != previous.speaker || word.start - previous.end >= rules.breakGap

535	                || current.count >= (style.maxWords ?? Int.max)

540	                current.append(word)

543	                current = Array(current[...mark])
544	                close(.clause)
545	                current = rest + [word]
546	            } else {
547	                close(.width)
548	                current = [word]
549	            }
550	        }
551	        close(.end)

553	        var cues: [CaptionLayout.Cue] = []
554	        for (index, page) in pages.enumerated() {
555	            let first = page.words[0]
556	            let last = page.words[page.words.count - 1]
557	            let end: Ticks
558	            if index + 1 < pages.count {
559	                let next = pages[index + 1].words[0].start
560	                end = next - last.end < rules.breakGap ? next : min(next, last.end + rules.hold)

562	                end = min(last.end + rules.hold, span.upperBound)
563	            }
564	            let lines = pager.lines(page.words) ?? [page.words]
565	            let text = lines.map { $0.map(\.text).joined(separator: " ") }

568	            var width: Double?

570	                (size, width) = pager.shrink(text)

572	            cues.append(
573	                CaptionLayout.Cue(
574	                    start: first.start, end: max(end, first.start), text: text,
575	                    tag: tag(at: first.start, clip: clip), words: page.words, size: size,
576	                    width: width))
577	        }
578	        return cues
579	    }

596	    /// The width arithmetic one run pages with: the style, its base size,
597	    /// the budget in pixels and the rules.
598	    private struct Pager {
599	        let style: CaptionStyle
600	        let size: Double
601	        let budget: Double
602	        let rules: Rules
603	
604	        static func endsSentence(_ text: String) -> Bool {
605	            guard let mark = text.last else { return false }
606	            return ".?!…".contains(mark)
607	        }
608	
609	        static func endsClause(_ text: String) -> Bool {
610	            guard let mark = text.last else { return false }
611	            return ",;:".contains(mark)
612	        }
613	
614	        func line(_ words: ArraySlice<CaptionCues.Word>) -> String {
615	            words.map(\.text).joined(separator: " ")
616	        }
617	
618	        /// The words laid greedily into at most `style.maxLines` lines, each
619	        /// within the budget — nil when they do not go. A line of one word
620	        /// wider than the budget is allowed only when it is the whole page:
621	        /// that is the lone word `shrink` answers for.
622	        func lines(_ words: [CaptionCues.Word]) -> [[CaptionCues.Word]]? {
623	            var out: [[CaptionCues.Word]] = []
624	            for word in words {
625	                if var last = out.last {
626	                    last.append(word)
627	                    if fits(line(last[...]), style: style, size: size, budget: budget) {
628	                        out[out.count - 1] = last
629	                        continue
630	                    }
631	                    guard out.count < style.maxLines else { return nil }
632	                }
633	                if words.count > 1, !fits(word.text, style: style, size: size, budget: budget) {
634	                    return nil
635	                }
636	                out.append([word])
637	            }
638	            return out
639	        }
640	
641	        /// The widest line of a page that lays, in pixels.
642	        func measure(_ words: [CaptionCues.Word]) -> Double {
643	            (lines(words) ?? [words]).map { width(line($0[...]), style, size) }.max() ?? 0
644	        }
645	
646	        /// Clause preference: a width break within `clauseWindow` words
647	        /// after a `,;:` moves back to the mark — when the page before it
648	        /// is at least `clauseMinimum` of the budget and what moves, with
649	        /// `word`, still lays. The index of the mark's word, or nil.
650	        func clauseMark(in page: [CaptionCues.Word], before word: CaptionCues.Word) -> Int? {
651	            let lowest = max(0, page.count - 1 - rules.clauseWindow)
652	            for mark in stride(from: page.count - 2, through: lowest, by: -1) {
653	                guard Self.endsClause(page[mark].text) else { continue }
654	                let head = Array(page[...mark])
655	                guard measure(head) >= rules.clauseMinimum * budget,
656	                      lines(Array(page[(mark + 1)...]) + [word]) != nil
657	                else { return nil }
658	                return mark
659	            }
660	            return nil
661	        }
662	
663	        /// The balance step, once per pair: when the page before the one
664	        /// just closed was closed by width alone, move its last word onto
665	        /// the new page if both still lay, no rule is broken, and their
666	        /// measured widths come closer. What stops a sentence ending on a
667	        /// one-word orphan while keeping every page within the budget.
668	        func balance(_ pages: inout [Page]) {
669	            guard pages.count >= 2 else { return }
670	            let before = pages[pages.count - 2]
671	            let after = pages[pages.count - 1]
672	            guard before.close == .width, before.words.count >= 2 else { return }
673	            let moved = before.words[before.words.count - 1]
674	            let kept = Array(before.words.dropLast())
675	            let grown = [moved] + after.words
676	            guard grown.count <= (style.maxWords ?? Int.max),
677	                  grown[grown.count - 1].end - moved.start <= rules.maxLength,
678	                  grown.allSatisfy({ $0.speaker == moved.speaker }),
679	                  lines(kept) != nil, lines(grown) != nil,
680	                  abs(measure(kept) - measure(grown))
681	                    < abs(measure(before.words) - measure(after.words))
682	            else { return }
683	            pages[pages.count - 2].words = kept
684	            pages[pages.count - 1].words = grown
685	        }
686	
687	        /// A lone word too wide for the budget: its size in 5 % steps of the
688	        /// base down to `shrinkFloor`, the first that fits — and when none
689	        /// does, the floor with `width = budget`, so CoreText wraps it.
690	        func shrink(_ text: String) -> (size: Double?, width: Double?) {
691	            let steps = Int(((1 - rules.shrinkFloor) / 0.05).rounded())
692	            for step in stride(from: 1, through: steps, by: 1) {
693	                let smaller = size * (1 - 0.05 * Double(step))
694	                if fits(text, style: style, size: smaller, budget: budget) {
695	                    return (smaller, nil)
696	                }
697	            }
698	            return (size * rules.shrinkFloor, budget)
699	        }
700	    }
701	}

3	/// Cues in, ops out — the half of caption import that has nothing to do with
4	/// SubRip, factored out of `CaptionImporter.swift` so the speech recogniser
5	/// (`Transcriber.swift`) lays its captions out exactly as an imported file's
6	/// are laid out. A caption is an ordinary text clip either way, and
7	/// `CaptionImporter`'s header doc is still where the reasoning for THAT lives.
8	///
9	/// **What is here is PLACEMENT, and only placement.** Road map 2 phase 4 says
10	/// the cue rules — at most two lines, at most 42 characters a line, at most
11	/// six seconds a cue, at least a frame between cues, and (road map 6 §5f) no
12	/// two speakers in one cue: five of them now — are "factored out
13	/// of `CaptionImporter.swift`". None of them was ever in that file: SubRip
14	/// supplies its own line breaks, the clip's `text.width` does the wrapping at
15	/// render time (`LayerRenderers.measure`), and the importer bounds no cue's
16	/// length. Moving those rules in here would silently re-wrap and re-time every
17	/// caption file people already import, and would break the 4b round trip
18	/// outright. So the five rules belong to the producer that has to invent line
19	/// breaks — the transcriber's cue builder — and this file does what the
20	/// importer actually did:
21	///
22	/// 1. snap each cue to the canvas frame grid (spec §5.1: the model never
23	///    stores a sub-frame time);
24	/// 2. give a cue that snapped to nothing its one frame back;
25	/// 3. sort by start, ties broken by the order the producer emitted them;
26	/// 4. cut an overlapping cue back to **abut** its successor — never to leave a
27	///    gap, because `b.start == a.end` is not an overlap (`transition.rs`), so
28	///    an abutting pair places cleanly and mints no `cross_dissolve`, while a
29	///    real overlap would both be refused by §6's rule and dissolve between two
30	///    captions if it were not;

247	    /// at the page's own size (a shrunk one or the style's), with its wrap
248	    /// width and its `words` in CLIP time — and puts the batch at the style's
249	    /// `y`, with the run's `looks` (W-15). `replacing` names caption tracks to remove
250	    /// WITH their clips in the same ops, first — `replaceableTracks` says
251	    /// which qualify — and the new track takes their place at the front.
252	    static func place(
253	        _ cues: [Cue], problems existing: [Problem] = [], in project: ReelProject,
254	        track: UInt32? = nil, trackBase: String = "Captions", style: CaptionStyle = .subtitles,
255	        looks: CaptionLooks = .none, replacing: [UInt32] = []
256	    ) throws -> Plan {
257	        let snapshot = project.snapshot
258	        let canvas = snapshot.canvas
259	        let frame = max(canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
260	        guard !cues.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.noCues(existing) }
261	
262	        // Snap, then give a cue that snapped to nothing its one frame back,
263	        // THEN resolve overlaps — in that order, so an overlap the minimum
264	        // length introduces is still one the overlap pass fixes.
265	        var placed = cues.enumerated().map { index, cue -> Placed in
266	            let start = ReelTime.snapToFrame(max(0, cue.start), fps: canvas.fps)
267	            let end = ReelTime.snapToFrame(cue.end, fps: canvas.fps)
268	            return Placed(
269	                tag: cue.tag, order: index, start: start, end: max(end, start + frame),
270	                text: cue.text, words: cue.words, size: cue.size, width: cue.width,
271	                speaker: cue.speaker)
272	        }
273	        placed.sort { $0.start == $1.start ? $0.order < $1.order : $0.start < $1.start }
274	
275	        // Captions are one track, so two cues on screen at once cannot both
276	        // be honoured: the later one wins its start and the earlier one is
277	        // cut back to it. That is also what the overlap rule (§6) would
278	        // otherwise refuse the placement over.
279	        var trimmed = 0
280	        for index in placed.indices.dropLast() where placed[index].end > placed[index + 1].start {
281	            placed[index].end = placed[index + 1].start
282	            trimmed += 1
283	        }
284	        var problems = existing
285	        for cue in placed where cue.end - cue.start < frame {
286	            problems.append(
287	                Problem(tag: cue.tag, reason: "starts less than a frame before the next caption"))
288	        }
289	        let kept = placed.filter { $0.end - $0.start >= frame }
290	        guard !kept.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.noCues(problems) }
291	
292	        // Before a single op: every op runs `Project::validate`, so a
293	        // transcript one clip too long would throw about clips, halfway
294	        // through, with the earlier ones already applied purely and thrown
295	        // away. The count is known here.
296	        let removed = Set(replacing)
297	        let room = Int(RC_MAX_CLIPS) - snapshot.clips.filter { !removed.contains($0.track) }.count
298	        guard kept.count <= room else {
299	            throw LayoutError.tooMany(cues: kept.count, room: max(0, room))
300	        }
301	
302	        // The replaced tracks go FIRST, clips and all: a removal mints no
303	        // id, so `next_id` below is still the new track's, and the new
304	        // track's index counts the stack as it will be once they are gone.
305	        var ops: [ReelOp] = replacing.map { .removeTrack(track: $0, withClips: true) }
306	        let destination: UInt32
307	        let name = trackName(in: snapshot, base: trackBase, excluding: replacing)
308	        if let track = track {
309	            destination = track
310	        } else {
311	            // A new id is `next_id` from BEFORE the op — the documented
312	            // contract of the one JSON entry point (§6), since an op returns
313	            // a project rather than an id. Index `tracks.count` is the front
314	            // of the stack, so captions draw over everything.
315	            destination = snapshot.nextId
316	            ops.append(.addTrack(index: snapshot.tracks.count - replacing.count, name: name))
317	        }
318	
319	        let preset = captionPreset
320	        let height = Double(canvas.height)
321	        let size = CGSize(width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height)
322	        var overTwoLines = 0
323	        if style.isWordStyle {
324	            let base = style.size(for: CGSize(width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height))
325	            for cue in kept {
326	                let words = cue.words.map { words in
327	                    words.map { TextWord(start: $0.start - cue.start, end: $0.end - cue.start) }
328	                }
329	                ops.append(
330	                    .addTextClip(
331	                        track: destination, at: cue.start, duration: cue.end - cue.start,
332	                        text: style.pagePatch(
333	                            content: cue.text, size: cue.size ?? base, width: cue.width,
334	                            words: words, looks: looks)))
335	            }
336	        } else {
337	            var base = TextPatch(
338	                font: preset.font, size: preset.size(on: size),
339	                align: preset.align, valign: "middle", backdrop: .some(preset.backdrop),
340	                width: .some(Double(canvas.width) * wrapFraction))
341	            if canvas.height > canvas.width {
342	                overTwoLines = kept.filter { measuresOverTwoLines($0.text, preset, on: size) }
343	                    .count
344	            }
345	            let colors = CaptionStyle.speakerColors(kept.map(\.speaker))
346	            for (cue, color) in zip(kept, colors) {
347	                base.content = cue.text
348	                base.color = color
349	                ops.append(
350	                    .addTextClip(
351	                        track: destination, at: cue.start, duration: cue.end - cue.start,
352	                        text: base))
353	            }
354	        }
355	
356	        // The preset's position is a `set_video` patch, and a patch needs
357	        // ids the ops have not minted yet — so the batch is applied PURELY
358	        // first and the ids read off the throwaway result. Applying the same
359	        // ops to the same handle mints the same ids, which is what makes
360	        // appending the patch to this very list correct
361	        // (`EditorViewController+AddClips.swift` does the same for one clip).
362	        //
363	        // The probe is kept rather than replaced by arithmetic on `next_id`:
364	        // ids ARE sequential when nothing is refused, and that is exactly the
365	        // invariant a refusal breaks — a caller-named track can refuse any
366	        // number of these placements, and then the patch would name clips
367	        // that do not exist.
368	        guard let probed = try project.applying(ops).project else { throw LayoutError.refused }
369	        let before = Set(snapshot.clips.map { $0.id })
370	        let created = probed.snapshot.clips.map { $0.id }.filter { !before.contains($0) }
371	        guard !created.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.refused }
372	        let at = preset.position(on: size)
373	        ops.append(
374	            .setVideo(
375	                clips: created,
376	                patch: style.isWordStyle
377	                    ? VideoPatch(x: 0, y: style.yFraction * height)
378	                    : VideoPatch(x: at.x, y: at.y, opacity: 1)))
379	
380	        return Plan(
381	            ops: ops, clips: created.count, cues: kept.count, trimmed: trimmed,
382	            problems: problems, trackName: track == nil ? name : nil, replaced: replacing,
383	            overTwoLines: overTwoLines)
384	    }
385	
386	    /// Whether a Subtitles cue, as `place` writes it on `canvas` (the Caption preset, its
387	    /// wrap box), measures taller than the same props holding two lines (spec §11 VR-41).
388	    static func measuresOverTwoLines(
389	        _ content: String, _ preset: TextPreset, on canvas: CGSize
390	    ) -> Bool {
391	        func props(_ text: String) -> TextProps {
392	            TextProps(
393	                content: text, font: preset.font, size: preset.size(on: canvas),
394	                align: preset.align, valign: "middle", backdrop: preset.backdrop,
395	                width: Double(canvas.width) * wrapFraction)
396	        }
397	        return LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for: props(content)).height
398	            > LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for: props("X\nX")).height
399	    }
400	
401	    /// The tracks a restyle may replace (road map 8 §5e's three rules): a
402	    /// track named as this file names caption tracks ("Captions",
403	    /// "Captions N"), holding at least one clip and only text clips, each overlapping
404	    /// some job's `span` — so nothing outside the run's scope is removed.
405	    static func replaceableTracks(
406	        in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, jobs: [Transcriber.Job]
407	    ) -> [UInt32] {
408	        snapshot.tracks.compactMap { track -> UInt32? in
409	            guard isCaptionTrackName(track.name) else { return nil }
410	            guard snapshot.clips.contains(where: { $0.track == track.id }) else { return nil }
411	            for clip in snapshot.clips where clip.track == track.id {
412	                guard case .text = clip.source else { return nil }
413	                let end = clip.start + clip.duration
414	                guard jobs.contains(where: { $0.span.overlaps(clip.start ..< end) }) else {
415	                    return nil
416	                }
417	            }
418	            return track.id
419	        }
420	    }
421	
422	    /// A name this file gives a caption track: "Captions" or "Captions N".
423	    static func isCaptionTrackName(_ name: String) -> Bool {
424	        if name == "Captions" { return true }
425	        guard name.hasPrefix("Captions ") else { return false }
426	        let suffix = name.dropFirst("Captions ".count)
427	        return !suffix.isEmpty && suffix.allSatisfy { $0.isASCII && $0.isNumber }
428	    }
429	
430	    /// "Captions", then "Captions 2" — so two runs are tellable apart in the
431	    /// track header. `base` is the producer's word for what it made, and both
432	    /// producers say "Captions": a transcript and an imported file are the
433	    /// same thing on the timeline, and a second name would only make the
434	    /// numbering restart.
435	    /// A track in `excluding` is one this plan removes, so its name is free.
436	    static func trackName(
437	        in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, base: String = "Captions", excluding: [UInt32] = []
438	    ) -> String {
439	        let taken = Set(snapshot.tracks.filter { !excluding.contains($0.id) }.map { $0.name })
440	        var name = base
441	        var suffix = 2
442	        while taken.contains(name) {
443	            name = "\(base) \(suffix)"
444	            suffix += 1
445	        }
446	        return name
447	    }
448	}
