452	/// Word caption pages re-paged from their own words on the current canvas (spec §11 VR-40):
453	/// what File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas and `relay_captions` do (VR-45), and step (6) of
454	/// Make Vertical (`VerticalVersion+Plan.swift`). W-7 and W-10 stand: `CaptionPages.repage` is
455	/// the measuring pager with lead 0 and `CaptionLayout.place` the one writer, so a re-laid page
456	/// is built exactly as a generated one is — from the words the pages hold, so every correction
457	/// is kept (the owner's answer, 2026-11-01).
458	///
459	/// `place(replacing:)` removes each replaced track with its clips first, so a track is
460	/// replaced only when every page on it is recognised: a track holding a page with no timings,
461	/// or in a style Frame Job does not make, is KEPT and named with its reason. Names no `rc_*`.
462	enum CaptionRelayout {
463	    /// The undo step's name (VR-45).
464	    static let actionName = "Re-lay Captions"
465	
466	    /// A caption track whose pages are all in one recognised style.
467	    struct Track: Equatable {
468	        let track: UInt32
469	        let name: String
470	        let style: CaptionStyle
471	        let looks: CaptionLooks
472	    }
473	
474	    /// A caption track left as placed, and why.
475	    struct Kept: Equatable {
476	        let track: UInt32
477	        let name: String
478	        let reason: String
479	    }
480	
481	    /// A track re-laid: the new track's id, the old one's, its name, style and page count.
482	    struct Relaid: Equatable {
483	        let track: UInt32
484	        let replaced: UInt32
485	        let name: String
486	        let style: CaptionStyle
487	        let pages: Int
488	    }
489	
490	    /// What the survey found, each list in stack order, back first.
491	    struct Survey: Equatable {
492	        let recognised: [Track]
493	        let kept: [Kept]
494	    }
495	
496	    struct Outcome: Equatable {
497	        var relaid: [Relaid]
498	        var kept: [Kept]
499	    }
500	
501	    /// VR-40 (a): the caption tracks of one container — named as `CaptionLayout` names them,
502	    /// holding at least one clip and only text clips — each recognised or kept with the first
503	    /// reason that applies.
504	    static func survey(_ snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Survey {
505	        var recognised: [Track] = []
506	        var kept: [Kept] = []
507	        for track in snapshot.tracks where CaptionLayout.isCaptionTrackName(track.name) {
508	            let clips = snapshot.clips(onTrack: track.id)
509	            guard !clips.isEmpty, clips.allSatisfy(isText) else { continue }
510	            func keep(_ reason: String) {
511	                kept.append(Kept(track: track.id, name: track.name, reason: reason))
512	            }
513	            if track.matte != .none {
514	                keep("it is a matte track")
515	                continue
516	            }
517	            let timed = clips.map { Self.words(of: $0) }
518	            if timed.contains(where: { $0 == nil }) {
519	                keep("it holds a page with no word timings")
520	                continue
521	            }
522	            if timed.contains(where: { $0?.isEmpty ?? true }) {
523	                keep("it holds a page none of whose words starts inside it")
524	                continue
525	            }
526	            let styles = clips.map { clip in clip.text.flatMap(recognise) }
527	            if styles.contains(where: { $0 == nil }) {
528	                keep("it holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make")
529	                continue
530	            }
531	            guard let first = styles[0],
532	                styles.allSatisfy({ $0?.style == first.style && $0?.looks == first.looks })
533	            else {
534	                keep("its pages are in more than one style")
535	                continue
536	            }
537	            recognised.append(
538	                Track(track: track.id, name: track.name, style: first.style, looks: first.looks))
539	        }
540	        return Survey(recognised: recognised, kept: kept)
541	    }
542	
543	    private static func isText(_ clip: ClipSnapshot) -> Bool {
544	        if case .text = clip.source { return true }
545	        return false
546	    }
547	
548	    /// VR-40 (b): the word style and looks a page was made in — its font the style's and its
549	    /// `word_style` the style's with those looks — or nil. Subtitles is never a match.
550	    static func recognise(_ text: TextProps) -> (style: CaptionStyle, looks: CaptionLooks)? {
551	        for style in CaptionStyle.allCases where style.isWordStyle && text.font == style.font {
552	            for bits in 0 ..< 8 {
553	                let looks = CaptionLooks(
554	                    slide: bits & 1 != 0, fill: bits & 2 != 0, dim: bits & 4 != 0)
555	                guard looks == looks.live(for: style) else { continue }
556	                if text.wordStyle == style.wordStyle(looks) { return (style, looks) }
557	            }
558	        }
559	        return nil
560	    }
561	
562	    /// VR-40 (c): a page's timed words in TIMELINE ticks, one per whitespace token of
563	    /// `content`, speaker nil — only those whose start lies inside the clip (a split's or a
564	    /// trim's half holds the words of the part it lost). Nil for a clip with no text, no
565	    /// words or a count that differs from the tokens; empty when none starts inside.
566	    static func words(of clip: ClipSnapshot) -> [CaptionCues.Word]? {
567	        guard let text = clip.text, !text.words.isEmpty else { return nil }
568	        let tokens = text.content.split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace)
569	        guard tokens.count == text.words.count else { return nil }
570	        let inside = clip.start ..< clip.start + clip.duration
571	        return zip(tokens, text.words).compactMap { token, word in
572	            let start = clip.start + word.start
573	            guard inside.contains(start) else { return nil }
574	            return CaptionCues.Word(
575	                text: String(token), start: start, end: clip.start + word.end, speaker: nil)
576	        }
577	    }
578	
579	    /// VR-40 (e): each track re-paged on the trial's canvas, back to front, as one batch per
580	    /// track tried op by op on a scratch copy; a `LayoutError` or a refusal keeps the track
581	    /// and applies nothing of it. Then the new track back at the old one's index, hidden and
582	    /// locked as it was. Throws only the core's invalid input.
583	    static func relay(_ tracks: [Track], on trial: inout SwitchAngle.Trial) throws -> Outcome {
584	        var outcome = Outcome(relaid: [], kept: [])
585	        for track in tracks {
586	            let before = trial.project.snapshot
587	            guard let index = before.tracks.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == track.track }) else {
588	                continue
589	            }
590	            let old = before.tracks[index]
591	            let canvas = CGSize(width: before.canvas.width, height: before.canvas.height)
592	            let frame = max(before.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
593	            let request = CaptionPages.Request(style: track.style, canvas: canvas)
594	            var cues: [CaptionLayout.Cue] = []
595	            for clip in before.clips(onTrack: track.track).sorted(by: { $0.start < $1.start }) {
596	                cues += CaptionPages.repage(
597	                    words(of: clip) ?? [], span: clip.start ..< clip.start + clip.duration,
598	                    frame: frame, request: request, clip: clip.id)
599	            }
600	            func keep(_ reason: String) {
601	                outcome.kept.append(Kept(track: track.track, name: track.name, reason: reason))
602	            }
603	            let plan: CaptionLayout.Plan
604	            do {
605	                plan = try CaptionLayout.place(
606	                    cues, in: trial.project, trackBase: track.name, style: track.style,
607	                    looks: track.looks, replacing: [track.track])
608	            } catch let error as CaptionLayout.LayoutError {
609	                keep(error.errorDescription ?? "the captions could not be placed")
610	                continue
611	            }
612	            var scratch = trial
613	            var refused: String?
614	            for op in plan.ops {
615	                if let why = try scratch.require(op) {
616	                    refused = why
617	                    break
618	                }
619	            }
620	            if let refused {
621	                keep(refused)
622	                continue
623	            }
624	            let known = Set(before.tracks.map(\.id))
625	            guard
626	                let made = scratch.project.snapshot.tracks.first(where: {
627	                    !known.contains($0.id)
628	                })
629	            else {
630	                keep("no caption track was made")
631	                continue
632	            }
633	            var follow: [ReelOp] = [.moveTrack(track: made.id, index: index)]
634	            if old.hidden { follow.append(.setTrack(track: made.id, hidden: true)) }
635	            if old.locked { follow.append(.setTrack(track: made.id, locked: true)) }
636	            for op in follow {
637	                if let why = try scratch.require(op) {
638	                    refused = why
639	                    break
640	                }
641	            }
642	            if let refused {
643	                keep(refused)
644	                continue
645	            }
646	            trial = scratch
647	            outcome.relaid.append(
648	                Relaid(
649	                    track: made.id, replaced: track.track, name: made.name, style: track.style,
650	                    pages: plan.clips))
651	        }
652	        return outcome
653	    }
654	
655	    /// VR-45: the survey and the re-lay of one container's handle (the editor's
656	    /// `editedProject`); the outcome's kept tracks are the survey's, then the re-lay's.
657	    static func plan(_ project: ReelProject) throws -> (ops: [ReelOp], outcome: Outcome) {
658	        let found = survey(project.snapshot)
659	        var trial = SwitchAngle.Trial(project: project)
660	        var outcome = try relay(found.recognised, on: &trial)
661	        outcome.kept = found.kept + outcome.kept
662	        return (trial.ops, outcome)
663	    }

665	    /// The answer's `relaid` and `kept`, as both tools spell them.
666	    static func answerFields(_ outcome: Outcome) -> [String: Any] {
667	        [
668	            "relaid": outcome.relaid.map { relaid -> [String: Any] in
669	                [
670	                    "track": Int(relaid.track), "replaced": Int(relaid.replaced),
671	                    "name": relaid.name, "style": relaid.style.rawValue, "pages": relaid.pages,
672	                ]
673	            },
674	            "kept": outcome.kept.map { kept -> [String: Any] in
675	                ["track": Int(kept.track), "name": kept.name, "reason": kept.reason]
676	            },
677	        ]
678	    }

680	    /// One kept track's line, as the notice and Make Vertical's summary say it.
681	    static func keptLine(_ kept: Kept) -> String {
682	        let why = kept.reason.hasSuffix(".") ? String(kept.reason.dropLast()) : kept.reason
683	        return "Caption track \"\(kept.name)\" is kept as placed: \(why)."
684	    }

686	    /// The menu's informational sheet: nil when nothing was kept.
687	    static func noticeText(_ outcome: Outcome) -> String? {
688	        guard !outcome.kept.isEmpty else { return nil }
689	        let count = outcome.relaid.count
690	        let head = count == 0
691	            ? "No caption track was re-laid."
692	            : "Re-laid \(count) caption track\(count == 1 ? "" : "s") for this canvas."
693	        return ([head] + outcome.kept.map(keptLine)).joined(separator: "\n")
694	    }

762	/// op tools that can change a clip's source map — `set_speed`,

373	    /// three orders of magnitude to spare, where 4096 × `Ticks.max` is not.
374	    static let maxSourceTicks: Ticks = 1_000_000_000_000_000
375	
376	    /// One offset in ticks, as a `Double`, landed in the clip — the ONE
377	    /// door both caption mappings convert through.
378	    ///
379	    /// The clamp is into `[0, duration]` and it happens in `Double`: an
380	    /// offset divided by a speed of 1e-300 is a finite `Double` far larger
381	    /// than `Ticks.max`, and `Ticks(_:)` on it traps rather than saturating.
382	    /// Rounded half away from zero, the rule both mappings had. NaN — which
383	    /// is what `0 / 0` answers when a word sits exactly on a zero-speed
384	    /// clip's `in` point — is 0, the clip's own start: the beginning of the
385	    /// clip is the one answer that is always inside it.
386	    static func placed(offset: Double, in job: Job) -> Ticks {
387	        guard !offset.isNaN else { return job.start }
388	        let bounded = min(max(offset, 0), Double(job.duration))
389	        return job.start + Ticks(bounded.rounded(.toNearestOrAwayFromZero))
390	    }

392	    // MARK: - What can be transcribed
393	
394	    /// Turns clips into jobs, and says why it refused the rest.
395	    ///
396	    /// Only a `media` clip whose file exists and has sound can be
397	    /// transcribed. A `still`, `image`, `text`, `shape` or `nest` source
398	    /// cannot — `edit.rs`'s non-media rule, in five names — and neither can a
399	    /// **reversed** clip, whose audio plays backwards and whose transcript
400	    /// would be nonsense presented as fact.
401	    ///
402	    /// "Has sound" is `InspectorTab.hasAudio`'s question and not the media's:
403	    /// the FILE having an audio track is only half of it, and `enabled.audio`
404	    /// is the other half (`audio.rs` gives such a clip no voice at all, so the
405	    /// timeline plays nothing for it). Detach Audio is what makes the
406	    /// difference visible — it leaves the picture clip with `enabled.audio`
407	    /// false and puts an audio-only twin with the SAME media, `in`, `start`
408	    /// and `speed` on the track below, so asking the media would recognise one
409	    /// recording twice, place two identical cues at one time, and then report
410	    /// the pile-up it made as captions that had to be shortened.
411	    ///
412	    /// The three-argument form is the instrument door old trees' probes
413	    /// build: it reads no map, so it refuses a clip whose speed ramps (spec
414	    /// §11 SR-20 (f)) rather than place its words at one rate.
415	    static func jobs(
416	        for clips: [ClipSnapshot], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, urls: [UInt32: URL]
417	    ) -> (jobs: [Job], problems: [CaptionLayout.Problem]) {
418	        jobs(for: clips, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: { _ in nil })
419	    }
420	
421	    /// `jobs(for:in:urls:)` with the source maps of the handle `snapshot`
422	    /// came from (spec §11 SR-20 (d)): a clip whose map is RAMPED gets its
423	    /// window from the map — `sourceIn` its first source tick, `sourceLength`
424	    /// what it reads, held to `maxSourceTicks` — and carries the map in
425	    /// `Job.ramp`; `speed` stays the base. A constant map, or none, is the
426	    /// old job exactly. A clip whose actions name `end.speed` with no ramped
427	    /// map is refused, by SR-20 (f)'s sentence.
428	    static func jobs(
429	        for clips: [ClipSnapshot], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, urls: [UInt32: URL],
430	        maps: SourceMaps
431	    ) -> (jobs: [Job], problems: [CaptionLayout.Problem]) {
432	        var jobs: [Job] = []
433	        var problems: [CaptionLayout.Problem] = []
434	        for clip in clips.sorted(by: { $0.start < $1.start }) {
435	            let tag = "clip \(clip.id)"
436	            guard case .media(let media, let sourceIn, let reversed) = clip.source else {
437	                problems.append(
438	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(
439	                        tag: tag, reason: "its source is not a media file, so it has no speech"))
440	                continue
441	            }
442	            guard !reversed else {
443	                problems.append(
444	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(
445	                        tag: tag,
446	                        reason: "it plays in reverse, so its speech cannot be transcribed"))
447	                continue
448	            }
449	            guard let entry = snapshot.media(media), entry.hasAudio else {
450	                problems.append(
451	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: tag, reason: "its media has no audio track"))
452	                continue
453	            }
454	            guard clip.enabled.audio else {
455	                problems.append(
456	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: tag, reason: "its audio is switched off"))
457	                continue
458	            }
459	            guard let url = urls[media] else {
460	                problems.append(
461	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: tag, reason: "its media file is missing"))
462	                continue
463	            }
464	            guard clip.speed.isFinite, clip.speed > 0, clip.duration > 0 else {
465	                problems.append(
466	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: tag, reason: "its speed or length is degenerate"))
467	                continue
468	            }
469	            let map = maps(clip.id).flatMap { $0.ramped ? $0 : nil }
470	            if map == nil, clip.actions.contains(where: { $0.end.speed != nil }) {
471	                problems.append(
472	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(
473	                        tag: tag, reason: "its speed ramps, and no speed map was read for it"))
474	                continue
475	            }
476	            if let map = map {
477	                jobs.append(
478	                    Job(
479	                        clip: clip.id, media: media, name: snapshot.name(of: clip), source: url,
480	                        sourceIn: min(max(0, map.sourceIn), maxSourceTicks),
481	                        sourceLength: min(map.sourceLength, maxSourceTicks),
482	                        start: clip.start, duration: clip.duration, speed: clip.speed,
483	                        ramp: Job.Ramp(map: map, clipStart: clip.start)))
484	                continue
485	            }
486	            jobs.append(
487	                Job(
488	                    clip: clip.id, media: media, name: snapshot.name(of: clip), source: url,
489	                    sourceIn: min(max(0, sourceIn), maxSourceTicks),
490	                    sourceLength: contentLength(of: clip),
491	                    start: clip.start, duration: clip.duration, speed: clip.speed))
492	        }
493	        return (jobs, problems)
494	    }
495	
496	    /// How much SOURCE time a clip plays — `Project::content_length_in_source`
497	    /// (`core/src/source_window.rs`) in Swift, because the extract's range is
498	    /// a source range and the core owns what that means.
499	    ///
500	    /// It does NOT saturate where the core saturates. The core's cast tops
501	    /// out at `i64::MAX`; this one tops out at `maxSourceTicks`, for the
502	    /// reason that constant's own doc gives — Swift sums this answer and the
503	    /// core does not. Every speed the ops can write (`SPEED_MIN`/`SPEED_MAX`)
504	    /// is orders of magnitude below the bound and answers exactly what it
505	    /// always did; R6-10 keeps it for speeds the reader now refuses (#41). The
506	    /// clamp is applied in `Double`: `Ticks(_:)` traps on an out-of-range
507	    /// one. The degenerate fallback is unchanged and is bounded too, since a
508	    /// hand-written `duration` can be as large as `Ticks` allows.
509	    ///
510	    /// A product that overflows to `+infinity` — which `duration × 1e308`
511	    /// does — is the bound and not the fallback: the honest answer to "how
512	    /// much source does this play" is "more than there can be", which is
513	    /// `maxSourceTicks`, where the clip's own duration would be a number
514	    /// pulled out of the air. `NaN`, a negative and `-infinity` all fail the
515	    /// `>= 1` test and take the fallback, as they always did.
516	    static func contentLength(of clip: ClipSnapshot) -> Ticks {
517	        let scaled = Double(clip.duration) * clip.speed
518	        guard scaled >= 1 else { return min(max(clip.duration, 1), maxSourceTicks) }
519	        return Ticks(min(scaled, Double(maxSourceTicks)).rounded())
520	    }
521	
522	    /// Whether anything in this project could be transcribed at all — the
523	    /// menu item's validator, deliberately the cheap snapshot question rather
524	    /// than a plan, because a validator runs on every menu open.
525	    ///
526	    /// It asks the same three things `jobs` asks and in the same order, minus
527	    /// the two a snapshot cannot answer without the document's media URLs, so
528	    /// the item can only be enabled where a run would find work. `enabled.audio`
529	    /// is one of the three: a timeline whose every audible clip has had its
530	    /// sound switched off has nothing to transcribe, and a menu item that
531	    /// opens a sheet whose only answer is "nothing to transcribe" is the
532	    /// dialog `generateCaptionsCommand`'s guard exists to prevent.
533	    static func hasTranscribableClip(in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
534	        snapshot.clips.contains { clip in
535	            guard case .media(let media, _, let reversed) = clip.source, !reversed,
536	                  clip.enabled.audio
537	            else {
538	                return false
539	            }
540	            return snapshot.media(media)?.hasAudio ?? false
541	        }
542	    }
543	}

557	/// The sheet's language popup and the tool's `language` argument: the
558	/// `Language` row, the two cached lists (`languages()`, the locales whose
559	/// model is INSTALLED on this Mac; `supportedLanguages()`, every locale the
560	/// engine names, each marked installed or not), the display-name builder
561	/// behind both, and the two lookups the callers use —
562	/// `defaultLanguage(in:)` for the popup's first selection and
563	/// `language(matching:in:)` for a tag a person or an agent typed.
564	///
565	/// Since W2 (spec §11 W-8) both lists are ASKED of `SpeechEngine`
566	/// (`supportedLocales()`, `installedLocales()`), never written down, and
567	/// every identifier is BCP-47 (`en-US`) — the engine answers `en_US`, and a
568	/// raw compare between the two spellings never matches. No transcriber is
569	/// constructed per locale here: constructing one reserves its locale against
570	/// a cap of 5 (W0 q3), so the installed SET comes from `installedLocales()`
571	/// and the one model question, `SpeechEngine.isInstalled`, is asked only for
572	/// the locale a run chose.
573	extension Transcriber {
574	
575	    // MARK: - Languages
576	
577	    /// One row of the sheet's language popup, and the vocabulary the tool's
578	    /// `language` argument speaks.
579	    struct Language: Equatable {
580	        /// A BCP-47 identifier, `en-US` — never `en_US`.
581	        let identifier: String
582	        let displayName: String
583	        /// Whether this Mac has the model. The sheet marks a row that has not
584	        /// and offers its Download row; a run refuses it.
585	        let installed: Bool
586	
587	        init(identifier: String, displayName: String, installed: Bool = true) {
588	            self.identifier = identifier
589	            self.displayName = displayName
590	            self.installed = installed
591	        }
592	
593	        var locale: Locale { Locale(identifier: identifier) }
594	    }
595	
596	    private static let languageLock = NSLock()
597	    private static var cachedLanguages: [Language]?
598	    private static var cachedSupported: [Language]?
599	
600	    /// Every locale whose model is INSTALLED on this Mac, sorted by display
601	    /// name — the rows a run can use without a download. All `installed`.
602	    ///
603	    /// Cached only when NON-empty: an empty answer is what `askBound`
604	    /// expiring looks like, and remembering it would make the feature refuse
605	    /// for the rest of the session on a Mac where it works.
606	    static func languages() -> [Language] {
607	        languageLock.lock()
608	        if let cached = cachedLanguages {
609	            languageLock.unlock()
610	            return cached
611	        }
612	        languageLock.unlock()
613	
614	        let found = named(SpeechEngine.installedLocales(), installed: nil)
615	        if !found.isEmpty {
616	            languageLock.lock()
617	            cachedLanguages = found
618	            languageLock.unlock()
619	        }
620	        return found
621	    }
622	
623	    /// Every locale the ENGINE names, model installed or not — the
624	    /// unfiltered twin of `languages()`, each row's `installed` read off the
625	    /// installed SET by BCP-47 tag.
626	    ///
627	    /// There are two lists because a caller who named a language this Mac
628	    /// could not use has one of TWO problems with two different fixes.
629	    /// `en-XX` is a tag the engine has never heard of, and the fix is to
630	    /// spell it right; `fr-FR` is a tag it knows that this Mac has no model
631	    /// for, and the fix is a person pressing Download in the sheet. Told only
632	    /// "this Mac cannot recognise it", somebody with the second problem
633	    /// retypes a tag that was right all along.
634	    ///
635	    /// Cached like its twin, and an empty answer is not cached — nor is a
636	    /// list read against an EMPTY installed set, which is what the installed
637	    /// ask expiring looks like: cached, every row would read "not installed"
638	    /// for the rest of the session.
639	    static func supportedLanguages() -> [Language] {
640	        languageLock.lock()
641	        if let cached = cachedSupported {
642	            languageLock.unlock()
643	            return cached
644	        }
645	        languageLock.unlock()
646	
647	        let installed = Set(SpeechEngine.installedLocales().map { $0.identifier(.bcp47) })
648	        let found = named(SpeechEngine.supportedLocales(), installed: installed)
649	        if !found.isEmpty, !installed.isEmpty {
650	            languageLock.lock()
651	            cachedSupported = found
652	            languageLock.unlock()
653	        }
654	        return found
655	    }
656	
657	    /// Drops both caches, so the next ask reads the engine again — what the
658	    /// sheet's Download row does once a model has been installed.
659	    static func forgetLanguages() {
660	        languageLock.lock()
661	        cachedLanguages = nil
662	        cachedSupported = nil
663	        languageLock.unlock()
664	    }
665	
666	    /// Locales as rows: tagged in BCP-47, named in this Mac's own language
667	    /// and sorted by that NAME rather than by tag, because a person reads the
668	    /// name — and both lists are built here so the popup and the two
669	    /// refusals cannot spell one locale two ways. `installed` nil means every
670	    /// row is installed; otherwise a row is installed when its tag is in it.
671	    /// A locale listed twice under one tag is one row.
672	    private static func named(_ locales: [Locale], installed: Set<String>?) -> [Language] {
673	        let names = Locale.current
674	        var seen = Set<String>()
675	        return locales.compactMap { locale -> Language? in
676	            let identifier = locale.identifier(.bcp47)
677	            guard seen.insert(identifier).inserted else { return nil }
678	            return Language(
679	                identifier: identifier,
680	                displayName: names.localizedString(forIdentifier: identifier) ?? identifier,
681	                installed: installed.map { $0.contains(identifier) } ?? true)
682	        }.sorted {
683	            $0.displayName.localizedStandardCompare($1.displayName) == .orderedAscending
684	        }
685	    }
686	
687	    /// The language a run defaults to: this Mac's own, then anything sharing
688	    /// its language code, then the first row — an INSTALLED row preferred at
689	    /// each step. Compared in BCP-47 (`Locale.current.identifier` is `en_US`
690	    /// and the rows are `en-US`). Over `languages()`, where every row is
691	    /// installed, this is exact → prefix → first.
692	    static func defaultLanguage(in list: [Language]) -> Language? {
693	        let current = Locale.current.identifier(.bcp47)
694	        func exact(_ row: Language) -> Bool {
695	            row.identifier.caseInsensitiveCompare(current) == .orderedSame
696	        }
697	        if let hit = list.first(where: { exact($0) && $0.installed }) { return hit }
698	        if let hit = list.first(where: exact) { return hit }
699	        let code = Locale.current.language.languageCode?.identifier ?? ""
700	        if !code.isEmpty {
701	            func near(_ row: Language) -> Bool { row.identifier.hasPrefix(code + "-") }
702	            if let hit = list.first(where: { near($0) && $0.installed }) { return hit }
703	            if let hit = list.first(where: near) { return hit }
704	        }
705	        return list.first(where: { $0.installed }) ?? list.first
706	    }
707	
708	    /// The language a caller named — `en-US`, `en`, or a display name — or nil
709	    /// when nothing in `list` matches it.
710	    ///
711	    /// It is asked of BOTH lists, and that is the point: of
712	    /// `supportedLanguages()` to tell a misspelling from a real tag, and then
713	    /// of `languages()` to tell a real tag this Mac has a model for from one
714	    /// it has not. Those are the tool's two language refusals, and one
715	    /// matcher answers both so they cannot come to disagree about what
716	    /// counts as a match.
717	    static func language(matching name: String, in list: [Language]) -> Language? {
718	        let wanted = name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
719	        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return nil }
720	        if let exact = list.first(where: {
721	            $0.identifier.caseInsensitiveCompare(wanted) == .orderedSame
722	        }) { return exact }
723	        if let named = list.first(where: {
724	            $0.displayName.caseInsensitiveCompare(wanted) == .orderedSame
725	        }) { return named }
726	        // `en` should find `en-US` — a caller who names a language rather
727	        // than a region means the one this Mac has.
728	        let prefix = wanted.replacingOccurrences(of: "_", with: "-").lowercased()
729	        return list.first { $0.identifier.lowercased().hasPrefix(prefix + "-") }
730	    }
731	}

26	/// **`run` is `Transcriber.run`'s twin line for line.** R6-7: no `async`

28	/// completion posted to main.

50	/// AssemblyAI as a second engine behind the one command (R6-1). Same jobs,
51	/// same cancel token, same frame, same `Outcome`, so
52	/// `TranscribeSheetController.finish` and the tool's placement code cannot
53	/// tell which engine ran.
54	final class CloudTranscriber {
55	
56	    enum AccessError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
57	        case credentialRequired
58	
59	        var errorDescription: String? {
60	            ModelKeys.sentence(.assemblyAI)
61	        }
62	    }
63	
64	    /// The serial queue the whole run happens on — `Transcriber.work`'s
65	    /// twin, and one of the queue seams app/CLAUDE.md lists. A run is
66	    /// network-bound minutes of somebody else's compute and must never be on
67	    /// main.
68	    private let work = DispatchQueue(label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.cloud-transcribe")
69	
70	    let client: AssemblyAIClient?
71	    /// Where `cache/transcripts/` lives for this run — the document's cache
72	    /// directory, passed by value so the run holds no document.
73	    let cacheDirectory: URL
74	    /// The media records the jobs point at, by id, for the stamp.
75	    let media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]
76	
77	    /// What the last run said. Written only inside `transcribe`, read only
78	    /// after it returns (or after `run`'s completion has fired), which is why
79	    /// it needs no lock: one run at a time on one serial queue, and the
80	    /// caller that reads it is the caller that waited for it.
81	    private(set) var report = Report()
82	
83	    init(client: AssemblyAIClient? = nil, cacheDirectory: URL, media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]) {
84	        self.client = client
85	        self.cacheDirectory = cacheDirectory
86	        self.media = media
87	    }
88	
89	    /// Transcribes every job and answers on the MAIN thread —
90	    /// `Transcriber.run`'s seam, so a sheet and a semaphore-waiting tool can
91	    /// both stay synchronous. `progress` is NOT hopped: it fires on the run's
92	    /// own queue and its caller bounces it.
93	    func run(
94	        jobs: [Transcriber.Job], options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool, frame: Ticks,
95	        pages: CaptionPages.Request, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken,
96	        progress: ((Double, String) -> Void)? = nil,
97	        completion: @escaping (Result<Transcriber.Outcome, any Error>) -> Void
98	    ) {
99	        work.async { [weak self] in
100	            guard let self = self else { return }
101	            let outcome = Result {
102	                try self.transcribe(
103	                    jobs, options: options, refresh: refresh, frame: frame, pages: pages,
104	                    cancel: cancel, progress: progress)
105	            }
106	            DispatchQueue.main.async { completion(outcome) }
107	        }
108	    }
109	
110	    /// `GET /v2/transcript?limit=1` on the run's OWN queue, answered on
111	    /// main — the Settings window's Verify button.
112	    ///
113	    /// Spec §11's R6-12: verify adds no queue. `work` is already one of the
114	    /// seams `app/CLAUDE.md` lists, and a second one for a single cheap
115	    /// authenticated GET would be a queue nobody could name a rule for.
116	    ///
117	    /// It captures the CLIENT and not `self`. A verify is a wait on a socket
118	    /// and the window that asked may be gone before it answers; there is
119	    /// nothing on this object for it to write, and a strong `self` would
120	    /// keep a whole transcriber alive for the duration of a button press.
121	    func verify(completion: @escaping (Result<Void, AssemblyAIClient.ClientError>) -> Void) {
122	        guard let client = self.client else {
123	            DispatchQueue.main.async {
124	                completion(.failure(.request(AccessError.credentialRequired.localizedDescription)))
125	            }
126	            return
127	        }
128	        work.async {
129	            let answer = client.verify()
130	            DispatchQueue.main.async { completion(answer) }
131	        }
132	    }
133	
134	    /// The synchronous body, road map 6 §5a. Call it off the main thread; a
135	    /// tool that already runs on the server thread calls it directly.
136	    ///
137	    /// There is no ceiling to report on the other side of a REST call, and
138	    /// since W2 there is none on this Mac either (spec §11 W-8): the tool's
139	    /// `truncated` key is gone for both engines, and the proof says so.
140	    func transcribe(
141	        _ jobs: [Transcriber.Job], options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool, frame: Ticks,
142	        pages: CaptionPages.Request, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken,
143	        progress: ((Double, String) -> Void)? = nil
144	    ) throws -> Transcriber.Outcome {
145	        report = Report()
146	        var last = 0.0
147	        func publish(_ value: Double, _ detail: String) {
148	            last = max(last, value)
149	            progress?(last, detail)
150	        }
151	        publish(0, "")
152	
153	        // (1) The janitor, FIRST on keyed runs — before anything this run does can
154	        // overwrite the file that holds an id we still owe a DELETE. A Stop
155	        // the person has ALREADY pressed is answered above it, and one that
156	        // arrives during it is heard between its items (the reader review,
157	        // §10.13 R1·2).
158	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
159	        if client == nil {
160	            report.janitorDeferred = MediaTranscript.undeleted(in: cacheDirectory).map(\.media)
161	        } else {
162	            let janitor = retryDeletes(cancel: cancel)
163	            report.janitorDeleted = janitor.deleted
164	            report.janitorFailed = janitor.failed
165	        }
166	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
167	        if client == nil, jobs.isEmpty || refresh { throw AccessError.credentialRequired }
168	
169	        // (2) Grouped by media, in the order of each media's FIRST clip, and
170	        // classified before any work starts so the progress shares are known.
171	        var order: [UInt32] = []
172	        var grouped: [UInt32: [Transcriber.Job]] = [:]
173	        for job in jobs {
174	            if grouped[job.media] == nil { order.append(job.media) }
175	            grouped[job.media, default: []].append(job)
176	        }
177	        // Admit the entire keyless batch from disk before deriving a cue.

137	    /// `MediaConsolidator.CancelToken`'s shape — one flag, one lock, safe from
138	    /// any thread and safe to set twice — with the running analysis under the
139	    /// same lock, because speech cancellation is PUSH: there is no loop of
140	    /// ours to poll inside a recognition, only `SpeechEngine.Handle.cancel()`.
141	    ///
142	    /// **It holds a `URLSessionTask` beside it** (road map 6 §5a), under the
143	    /// same lock and cancelled outside it, for the same reason: a cloud run
144	    /// waiting on an upload has no loop of its own either, and one token has
145	    /// to stop whichever engine is running. The two slots are independent —
146	    /// only one engine runs at a time, and a token that had to know which
147	    /// would be a token every caller had to tell.
148	    final class CancelToken {
149	        private let lock = NSLock()
150	        private var flag = false
151	        private var task: SpeechEngine.Handle?
152	        private var request: URLSessionTask?
153	
154	        var isCancelled: Bool {
155	            lock.lock()
156	            defer { lock.unlock() }
157	            return flag
158	        }
159	
160	        func cancel() {
161	            lock.lock()
162	            flag = true
163	            let running = task
164	            let sending = request
165	            lock.unlock()
166	            // Outside the lock: `cancel()` reaches into the engine's task —
167	            // and, for a `URLSessionTask`, the session's delegate — and
168	            // holding a lock across it would be a lock held across somebody
169	            // else's code.
170	            running?.cancel()
171	            sending?.cancel()
172	        }
173	
174	        /// Stops the task that is running WITHOUT marking the run cancelled —
175	        /// what a wedged recognition earns. The flag is the run's, and a job
176	        /// that timed out must not set it: every later job would then refuse
177	        /// as cancelled and the whole outcome, earlier clips included, would
178	        /// be thrown away over one clip the recogniser never finished.
179	        func stopTask() {
180	            lock.lock()
181	            let running = task
182	            let sending = request
183	            lock.unlock()
184	            running?.cancel()
185	            sending?.cancel()
186	        }
187	
188	        /// Hands the token the analysis it may stop. A cancel that arrived
189	        /// while the analysis was being created still lands.
190	        func attach(_ task: SpeechEngine.Handle?) {
191	            lock.lock()
192	            self.task = task
193	            let already = flag
194	            lock.unlock()
195	            if already { task?.cancel() }
196	        }
197	
198	        /// The cloud run's half of the same contract, and an overload rather
199	        /// than a second name so a caller that holds a token cancels it the
200	        /// one way whatever is running underneath.
201	        func attach(_ task: URLSessionTask?) {
202	            lock.lock()
203	            self.request = task
204	            let already = flag
205	            lock.unlock()
206	            if already { task?.cancel() }
207	        }
208	
209	        func release() {
210	            lock.lock()
211	            task = nil
212	            request = nil
213	            lock.unlock()
214	        }
215	    }

335	/// What a run is given to do: `jobs(for:in:urls:)`, which turns the clips a
336	/// caller named into `Job`s and says in `CaptionLayout.Problem`'s vocabulary
337	/// why it refused the rest, `contentLength(of:)`, the one place a clip's
338	/// source window is measured for them, and `hasTranscribableClip(in:)`, the
339	/// cheap question the menu's validator asks.
340	///
341	/// It arrived as a pure move out of `Transcriber.swift` (road map 6's C1
342	/// toll 1), and it is no longer one: c1-run added `maxSourceTicks`, the
343	/// bound on `Job.sourceIn`, the clamp inside `contentLength(of:)` and
344	/// `placed(offset:in:)`, the one door every `Double → Ticks` conversion on
345	/// the caption path goes through. One widening survives from the move:
346	/// `contentLength(of:)` is internal rather than `private` (road map 6 §5h
347	/// names it), which no compiler error demanded — its one caller, `jobs`,
348	/// moved with it.
349	///
350	/// **Why anything here is bounded at all — spec §11's R6-10.** A clip's
351	/// `speed` is bounded to `SPEED_MIN`/`SPEED_MAX` by the OPS
352	/// (`core/src/edit_clip_timing.rs`: `set_speed` clamps, `rate_stretch` is an
353	/// identity outside) and, since R6-10's amendment (#41), by the reader too
354	/// — `Project::validate`'s `check_clips` refuses a clip outside them — so
355	/// no opened project reaches this code with a tiny or huge speed. The
356	/// clamps here stay as the second layer R6-10 keeps, because if one ever
357	/// did, the two ends of the arithmetic would fail in two places: a huge
358	/// speed overflows the SOURCE LENGTH here, and a tiny one overflows the
359	/// OFFSET in the two mappings. Both clamp in `Double`, before the
360	/// conversion, because a `Ticks(_:)` on an out-of-range `Double` traps.
361	extension Transcriber {
362	
363	    /// The ceiling on any source time this file answers: 1e15 ticks, about
364	    /// 1.9 billion seconds, some fifty years of media.
365	    ///
366	    /// Deliberately NOT `Ticks.max`, which is what the core's own
367	    /// `content_length_in_source` saturates at (`core/src/source_window.rs`
368	    /// casts an `f64` and an out-of-range cast saturates in Rust rather than
369	    /// trapping). The core never ADDS that number to anything; Swift does.
370	    /// `MediaTranscript.words` adds it to `sourceIn` for the window's end,
371	    /// and `TranscribeSheetController.refresh` sums it over every job, at
372	    /// most `MAX_CLIPS` = 4096 of them — and 4096 × 1e15 is under 2^63 with
373	    /// three orders of magnitude to spare, where 4096 × `Ticks.max` is not.
374	    static let maxSourceTicks: Ticks = 1_000_000_000_000_000
375	
376	    /// One offset in ticks, as a `Double`, landed in the clip — the ONE
377	    /// door both caption mappings convert through.
378	    ///
379	    /// The clamp is into `[0, duration]` and it happens in `Double`: an
380	    /// offset divided by a speed of 1e-300 is a finite `Double` far larger
381	    /// than `Ticks.max`, and `Ticks(_:)` on it traps rather than saturating.
382	    /// Rounded half away from zero, the rule both mappings had. NaN — which
383	    /// is what `0 / 0` answers when a word sits exactly on a zero-speed
384	    /// clip's `in` point — is 0, the clip's own start: the beginning of the
385	    /// clip is the one answer that is always inside it.
386	    static func placed(offset: Double, in job: Job) -> Ticks {
387	        guard !offset.isNaN else { return job.start }
388	        let bounded = min(max(offset, 0), Double(job.duration))
389	        return job.start + Ticks(bounded.rounded(.toNearestOrAwayFromZero))
390	    }

394	    /// Turns clips into jobs, and says why it refused the rest.
395	    ///
396	    /// Only a `media` clip whose file exists and has sound can be
397	    /// transcribed. A `still`, `image`, `text`, `shape` or `nest` source
398	    /// cannot — `edit.rs`'s non-media rule, in five names — and neither can a
399	    /// **reversed** clip, whose audio plays backwards and whose transcript
400	    /// would be nonsense presented as fact.
401	    ///
402	    /// "Has sound" is `InspectorTab.hasAudio`'s question and not the media's:
403	    /// the FILE having an audio track is only half of it, and `enabled.audio`
404	    /// is the other half (`audio.rs` gives such a clip no voice at all, so the
405	    /// timeline plays nothing for it). Detach Audio is what makes the
406	    /// difference visible — it leaves the picture clip with `enabled.audio`
407	    /// false and puts an audio-only twin with the SAME media, `in`, `start`
408	    /// and `speed` on the track below, so asking the media would recognise one
409	    /// recording twice, place two identical cues at one time, and then report
410	    /// the pile-up it made as captions that had to be shortened.
411	    ///
412	    /// The three-argument form is the instrument door old trees' probes
413	    /// build: it reads no map, so it refuses a clip whose speed ramps (spec
414	    /// §11 SR-20 (f)) rather than place its words at one rate.
415	    static func jobs(
416	        for clips: [ClipSnapshot], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, urls: [UInt32: URL]
417	    ) -> (jobs: [Job], problems: [CaptionLayout.Problem]) {
418	        jobs(for: clips, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: { _ in nil })
419	    }

421	    /// `jobs(for:in:urls:)` with the source maps of the handle `snapshot`
422	    /// came from (spec §11 SR-20 (d)): a clip whose map is RAMPED gets its
423	    /// window from the map — `sourceIn` its first source tick, `sourceLength`
424	    /// what it reads, held to `maxSourceTicks` — and carries the map in
425	    /// `Job.ramp`; `speed` stays the base. A constant map, or none, is the
426	    /// old job exactly. A clip whose actions name `end.speed` with no ramped
427	    /// map is refused, by SR-20 (f)'s sentence.
428	    static func jobs(
429	        for clips: [ClipSnapshot], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, urls: [UInt32: URL],
430	        maps: SourceMaps
431	    ) -> (jobs: [Job], problems: [CaptionLayout.Problem]) {
432	        var jobs: [Job] = []
433	        var problems: [CaptionLayout.Problem] = []
434	        for clip in clips.sorted(by: { $0.start < $1.start }) {
435	            let tag = "clip \(clip.id)"
436	            guard case .media(let media, let sourceIn, let reversed) = clip.source else {
437	                problems.append(
438	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(
439	                        tag: tag, reason: "its source is not a media file, so it has no speech"))
440	                continue
441	            }
442	            guard !reversed else {
443	                problems.append(
444	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(
445	                        tag: tag,
446	                        reason: "it plays in reverse, so its speech cannot be transcribed"))
447	                continue
448	            }
449	            guard let entry = snapshot.media(media), entry.hasAudio else {
450	                problems.append(
451	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: tag, reason: "its media has no audio track"))
452	                continue
453	            }
454	            guard clip.enabled.audio else {
455	                problems.append(
456	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: tag, reason: "its audio is switched off"))
457	                continue
458	            }
459	            guard let url = urls[media] else {
460	                problems.append(
461	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: tag, reason: "its media file is missing"))
462	                continue
463	            }
464	            guard clip.speed.isFinite, clip.speed > 0, clip.duration > 0 else {
465	                problems.append(
466	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: tag, reason: "its speed or length is degenerate"))
467	                continue
468	            }
469	            let map = maps(clip.id).flatMap { $0.ramped ? $0 : nil }
470	            if map == nil, clip.actions.contains(where: { $0.end.speed != nil }) {
471	                problems.append(
472	                    CaptionLayout.Problem(
473	                        tag: tag, reason: "its speed ramps, and no speed map was read for it"))
474	                continue
475	            }
476	            if let map = map {
477	                jobs.append(
478	                    Job(
479	                        clip: clip.id, media: media, name: snapshot.name(of: clip), source: url,
480	                        sourceIn: min(max(0, map.sourceIn), maxSourceTicks),
481	                        sourceLength: min(map.sourceLength, maxSourceTicks),
482	                        start: clip.start, duration: clip.duration, speed: clip.speed,
483	                        ramp: Job.Ramp(map: map, clipStart: clip.start)))
484	                continue
485	            }
486	            jobs.append(
487	                Job(
488	                    clip: clip.id, media: media, name: snapshot.name(of: clip), source: url,
489	                    sourceIn: min(max(0, sourceIn), maxSourceTicks),
490	                    sourceLength: contentLength(of: clip),
491	                    start: clip.start, duration: clip.duration, speed: clip.speed))
492	        }
493	        return (jobs, problems)

496	    /// How much SOURCE time a clip plays — `Project::content_length_in_source`
497	    /// (`core/src/source_window.rs`) in Swift, because the extract's range is
498	    /// a source range and the core owns what that means.
499	    ///
500	    /// It does NOT saturate where the core saturates. The core's cast tops
501	    /// out at `i64::MAX`; this one tops out at `maxSourceTicks`, for the
502	    /// reason that constant's own doc gives — Swift sums this answer and the
503	    /// core does not. Every speed the ops can write (`SPEED_MIN`/`SPEED_MAX`)
504	    /// is orders of magnitude below the bound and answers exactly what it
505	    /// always did; R6-10 keeps it for speeds the reader now refuses (#41). The
506	    /// clamp is applied in `Double`: `Ticks(_:)` traps on an out-of-range
507	    /// one. The degenerate fallback is unchanged and is bounded too, since a
508	    /// hand-written `duration` can be as large as `Ticks` allows.
509	    ///
510	    /// A product that overflows to `+infinity` — which `duration × 1e308`
511	    /// does — is the bound and not the fallback: the honest answer to "how
512	    /// much source does this play" is "more than there can be", which is
513	    /// `maxSourceTicks`, where the clip's own duration would be a number
514	    /// pulled out of the air. `NaN`, a negative and `-infinity` all fail the
515	    /// `>= 1` test and take the fallback, as they always did.
516	    static func contentLength(of clip: ClipSnapshot) -> Ticks {
517	        let scaled = Double(clip.duration) * clip.speed
518	        guard scaled >= 1 else { return min(max(clip.duration, 1), maxSourceTicks) }
519	        return Ticks(min(scaled, Double(maxSourceTicks)).rounded())
520	    }

609	            languageLock.unlock()
610	            return cached
611	        }
612	        languageLock.unlock()
613	
614	        let found = named(SpeechEngine.installedLocales(), installed: nil)
615	        if !found.isEmpty {
616	            languageLock.lock()
617	            cachedLanguages = found
618	            languageLock.unlock()
619	        }
620	        return found
621	    }
622	
623	    /// Every locale the ENGINE names, model installed or not — the
624	    /// unfiltered twin of `languages()`, each row's `installed` read off the
625	    /// installed SET by BCP-47 tag.
626	    ///
627	    /// There are two lists because a caller who named a language this Mac
628	    /// could not use has one of TWO problems with two different fixes.
629	    /// `en-XX` is a tag the engine has never heard of, and the fix is to
630	    /// spell it right; `fr-FR` is a tag it knows that this Mac has no model
631	    /// for, and the fix is a person pressing Download in the sheet. Told only
632	    /// "this Mac cannot recognise it", somebody with the second problem
633	    /// retypes a tag that was right all along.
634	    ///
635	    /// Cached like its twin, and an empty answer is not cached — nor is a
636	    /// list read against an EMPTY installed set, which is what the installed
637	    /// ask expiring looks like: cached, every row would read "not installed"
638	    /// for the rest of the session.
639	    static func supportedLanguages() -> [Language] {
640	        languageLock.lock()
641	        if let cached = cachedSupported {
642	            languageLock.unlock()
643	            return cached
644	        }
645	        languageLock.unlock()
646	
647	        let installed = Set(SpeechEngine.installedLocales().map { $0.identifier(.bcp47) })
648	        let found = named(SpeechEngine.supportedLocales(), installed: installed)
649	        if !found.isEmpty, !installed.isEmpty {
650	            languageLock.lock()
651	            cachedSupported = found
652	            languageLock.unlock()
653	        }
654	        return found
655	    }
656	
657	    /// Drops both caches, so the next ask reads the engine again — what the
658	    /// sheet's Download row does once a model has been installed.
659	    static func forgetLanguages() {
660	        languageLock.lock()
661	        cachedLanguages = nil
662	        cachedSupported = nil
663	        languageLock.unlock()
664	    }
665	
666	    /// Locales as rows: tagged in BCP-47, named in this Mac's own language
667	    /// and sorted by that NAME rather than by tag, because a person reads the
668	    /// name — and both lists are built here so the popup and the two
669	    /// refusals cannot spell one locale two ways. `installed` nil means every
670	    /// row is installed; otherwise a row is installed when its tag is in it.
671	    /// A locale listed twice under one tag is one row.
672	    private static func named(_ locales: [Locale], installed: Set<String>?) -> [Language] {
673	        let names = Locale.current
674	        var seen = Set<String>()
675	        return locales.compactMap { locale -> Language? in
676	            let identifier = locale.identifier(.bcp47)
677	            guard seen.insert(identifier).inserted else { return nil }
678	            return Language(
679	                identifier: identifier,
680	                displayName: names.localizedString(forIdentifier: identifier) ?? identifier,
681	                installed: installed.map { $0.contains(identifier) } ?? true)
682	        }.sorted {
683	            $0.displayName.localizedStandardCompare($1.displayName) == .orderedAscending
684	        }
685	    }
686	
687	    /// The language a run defaults to: this Mac's own, then anything sharing
688	    /// its language code, then the first row — an INSTALLED row preferred at
689	    /// each step. Compared in BCP-47 (`Locale.current.identifier` is `en_US`
690	    /// and the rows are `en-US`). Over `languages()`, where every row is
691	    /// installed, this is exact → prefix → first.
692	    static func defaultLanguage(in list: [Language]) -> Language? {
693	        let current = Locale.current.identifier(.bcp47)
694	        func exact(_ row: Language) -> Bool {
695	            row.identifier.caseInsensitiveCompare(current) == .orderedSame
696	        }
697	        if let hit = list.first(where: { exact($0) && $0.installed }) { return hit }
698	        if let hit = list.first(where: exact) { return hit }
699	        let code = Locale.current.language.languageCode?.identifier ?? ""
700	        if !code.isEmpty {
701	            func near(_ row: Language) -> Bool { row.identifier.hasPrefix(code + "-") }
702	            if let hit = list.first(where: { near($0) && $0.installed }) { return hit }
703	            if let hit = list.first(where: near) { return hit }
704	        }
705	        return list.first(where: { $0.installed }) ?? list.first
706	    }
707	
708	    /// The language a caller named — `en-US`, `en`, or a display name — or nil
709	    /// when nothing in `list` matches it.
710	    ///
711	    /// It is asked of BOTH lists, and that is the point: of
712	    /// `supportedLanguages()` to tell a misspelling from a real tag, and then
713	    /// of `languages()` to tell a real tag this Mac has a model for from one
714	    /// it has not. Those are the tool's two language refusals, and one
715	    /// matcher answers both so they cannot come to disagree about what
716	    /// counts as a match.
717	    static func language(matching name: String, in list: [Language]) -> Language? {
718	        let wanted = name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
719	        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return nil }
720	        if let exact = list.first(where: {
721	            $0.identifier.caseInsensitiveCompare(wanted) == .orderedSame
722	        }) { return exact }
723	        if let named = list.first(where: {
724	            $0.displayName.caseInsensitiveCompare(wanted) == .orderedSame
725	        }) { return named }
726	        // `en` should find `en-US` — a caller who names a language rather
727	        // than a region means the one this Mac has.
728	        let prefix = wanted.replacingOccurrences(of: "_", with: "-").lowercased()
729	        return list.first { $0.identifier.lowercased().hasPrefix(prefix + "-") }
730	    }
731	}

26	/// **`run` is `Transcriber.run`'s twin line for line.** R6-7: no `async`
27	/// here or below it, one serial queue, the body synchronous on it, the single

40	    /// person is choosing is where their audio goes, not whose recogniser it

57	        case credentialRequired
58	
59	        var errorDescription: String? {
60	            ModelKeys.sentence(.assemblyAI)
61	        }
62	    }
63	
64	    /// The serial queue the whole run happens on — `Transcriber.work`'s
65	    /// twin, and one of the queue seams app/CLAUDE.md lists. A run is
66	    /// network-bound minutes of somebody else's compute and must never be on
67	    /// main.
68	    private let work = DispatchQueue(label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.cloud-transcribe")
69	
70	    let client: AssemblyAIClient?
71	    /// Where `cache/transcripts/` lives for this run — the document's cache

73	    let cacheDirectory: URL
74	    /// The media records the jobs point at, by id, for the stamp.
75	    let media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]

77	    /// What the last run said. Written only inside `transcribe`, read only
78	    /// after it returns (or after `run`'s completion has fired), which is why
79	    /// it needs no lock: one run at a time on one serial queue, and the
80	    /// caller that reads it is the caller that waited for it.
81	    private(set) var report = Report()
82	
83	    init(client: AssemblyAIClient? = nil, cacheDirectory: URL, media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]) {
84	        self.client = client
85	        self.cacheDirectory = cacheDirectory
86	        self.media = media
87	    }
88	
89	    /// Transcribes every job and answers on the MAIN thread —
90	    /// `Transcriber.run`'s seam, so a sheet and a semaphore-waiting tool can
91	    /// both stay synchronous. `progress` is NOT hopped: it fires on the run's
92	    /// own queue and its caller bounces it.
93	    func run(
94	        jobs: [Transcriber.Job], options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool, frame: Ticks,
95	        pages: CaptionPages.Request, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken,
96	        progress: ((Double, String) -> Void)? = nil,
97	        completion: @escaping (Result<Transcriber.Outcome, any Error>) -> Void
98	    ) {
99	        work.async { [weak self] in
100	            guard let self = self else { return }
101	            let outcome = Result {
102	                try self.transcribe(
103	                    jobs, options: options, refresh: refresh, frame: frame, pages: pages,
104	                    cancel: cancel, progress: progress)
105	            }
106	            DispatchQueue.main.async { completion(outcome) }
107	        }
108	    }
109	
110	    /// `GET /v2/transcript?limit=1` on the run's OWN queue, answered on
111	    /// main — the Settings window's Verify button.
112	    ///
113	    /// Spec §11's R6-12: verify adds no queue. `work` is already one of the
114	    /// seams `app/CLAUDE.md` lists, and a second one for a single cheap
115	    /// authenticated GET would be a queue nobody could name a rule for.
116	    ///
117	    /// It captures the CLIENT and not `self`. A verify is a wait on a socket
118	    /// and the window that asked may be gone before it answers; there is
119	    /// nothing on this object for it to write, and a strong `self` would
120	    /// keep a whole transcriber alive for the duration of a button press.
121	    func verify(completion: @escaping (Result<Void, AssemblyAIClient.ClientError>) -> Void) {
122	        guard let client = self.client else {
123	            DispatchQueue.main.async {
124	                completion(.failure(.request(AccessError.credentialRequired.localizedDescription)))
125	            }
126	            return
127	        }
128	        work.async {
129	            let answer = client.verify()
130	            DispatchQueue.main.async { completion(answer) }
131	        }
132	    }
133	
134	    /// The synchronous body, road map 6 §5a. Call it off the main thread; a
135	    /// tool that already runs on the server thread calls it directly.
136	    ///
137	    /// There is no ceiling to report on the other side of a REST call, and
138	    /// since W2 there is none on this Mac either (spec §11 W-8): the tool's
139	    /// `truncated` key is gone for both engines, and the proof says so.
140	    func transcribe(
141	        _ jobs: [Transcriber.Job], options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool, frame: Ticks,
142	        pages: CaptionPages.Request, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken,
143	        progress: ((Double, String) -> Void)? = nil
144	    ) throws -> Transcriber.Outcome {
145	        report = Report()
146	        var last = 0.0
147	        func publish(_ value: Double, _ detail: String) {
148	            last = max(last, value)
149	            progress?(last, detail)
150	        }
151	        publish(0, "")
152	
153	        // (1) The janitor, FIRST on keyed runs — before anything this run does can
154	        // overwrite the file that holds an id we still owe a DELETE. A Stop
155	        // the person has ALREADY pressed is answered above it, and one that
156	        // arrives during it is heard between its items (the reader review,
157	        // §10.13 R1·2).
158	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
159	        if client == nil {
160	            report.janitorDeferred = MediaTranscript.undeleted(in: cacheDirectory).map(\.media)
161	        } else {
162	            let janitor = retryDeletes(cancel: cancel)
163	            report.janitorDeleted = janitor.deleted
164	            report.janitorFailed = janitor.failed
165	        }
166	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
167	        if client == nil, jobs.isEmpty || refresh { throw AccessError.credentialRequired }
168	
169	        // (2) Grouped by media, in the order of each media's FIRST clip, and
170	        // classified before any work starts so the progress shares are known.
171	        var order: [UInt32] = []
172	        var grouped: [UInt32: [Transcriber.Job]] = [:]
173	        for job in jobs {
174	            if grouped[job.media] == nil { order.append(job.media) }
175	            grouped[job.media, default: []].append(job)
176	        }
177	        // Admit the entire keyless batch from disk before deriving a cue.
178	        // Holding these decoded files also closes the gap between admission
179	        // and use if a package file disappears while the worker is running.
180	        var keylessFiles: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File] = [:]
181	        if client == nil {
182	            for id in order {
183	                if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
184	                guard let entry = media[id], let url = grouped[id]?.first?.source,
185	                    let source = MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: entry, url: url),
186	                    MediaTranscript.readStamp(for: id, in: cacheDirectory)?.serves(
187	                        TranscriptStamp(source: source, options: options), for: .captions) == true,
188	                    let file = MediaTranscript.read(for: id, in: cacheDirectory)
189	                else { throw AccessError.credentialRequired }
190	                keylessFiles[id] = file
191	            }
192	            report.cached = order
193	        }
194	        var stamps: [UInt32: TranscriptStamp] = [:]
195	        var unreadable: [UInt32] = []
196	        var toUpload: [UInt32] = []
197	        var held: [UInt32] = []
198	        var cached: [UInt32] = []
199	        for id in order {
200	            if client == nil { continue }
201	            guard let entry = media[id], let url = grouped[id]?.first?.source,
202	                let source = MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: entry, url: url)
203	            else {
204	                unreadable.append(id)
205	                continue
206	            }
207	            let stamp = TranscriptStamp(source: source, options: options)
208	            stamps[id] = stamp
209	            if MediaTranscript.isCurrent(stamp, for: id, in: cacheDirectory), !refresh {
210	                cached.append(id)
211	            } else if report.janitorFailed.contains(id) {
212	                held.append(id)
213	            } else {
214	                toUpload.append(id)
215	            }
216	        }
217	        report.held = held
218	        // Held and cached media are NOT in the shares: neither costs a
219	        // second of work, and a slice for one would make the bar stall.
220	        let bar = CloudProgress(seconds: toUpload.map { ReelTime.seconds(media[$0]?.duration ?? 0) })
221	
222	        var files: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File] = [:]
223	        var cues: [CaptionLayout.Cue] = []
224	        var problems: [CaptionLayout.Problem] = []
225	        var clips: [UInt32] = []
226	        // Kept apart from `problems` for `Transcriber.transcribe`'s reason:
227	        // they decide WHICH refusal an empty run earns.
228	        var failures: [String] = []
229	
230	        func refuse(_ id: UInt32, _ reason: String) {
231	            for job in grouped[id] ?? [] {
232	                problems.append(CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: "clip \(job.clip)", reason: reason))
233	                failures.append("clip \(job.clip): \(reason)")
234	            }
235	        }
236	
237	        for id in order {
238	            if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
239	            if let file = keylessFiles[id] {
240	                files[id] = file
241	            } else if unreadable.contains(id) {
242	                refuse(id, "its media file could not be read")
243	            } else if cached.contains(id) {
244	                if let file = MediaTranscript.read(for: id, in: cacheDirectory) {
245	                    files[id] = file
246	                    report.cached.append(id)
247	                } else {
248	                    refuse(id, "its cached transcript could not be read")
249	                }
250	            } else if held.contains(id) {
251	                // R6-11, the whole of it: no fetch, no write, one sentence
252	                // per clip, and the file left byte for byte.
253	                refuse(
254	                    id,
255	                    "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting its earlier transcript, so it was "
256	                        + "not uploaded again; the next run with an API key retries the delete")
257	            } else if let index = toUpload.firstIndex(of: id), let entry = media[id],
258	                let url = grouped[id]?.first?.source, let stamp = stamps[id]
259	            {
260	                do {
261	                    let answer = try fetch(
262	                        media: entry, url: url, stamp: stamp, options: options, cancel: cancel,
263	                        progress: { phase, within, detail in
264	                            publish(bar.fraction(media: index, phase: phase, within: within), detail)
265	                        })
266	                    files[id] = answer.file
267	                    report.uploaded.append(answer.uploaded)
268	                    publish(
269	                        bar.fraction(media: index, phase: .saving, within: 1),
270	                        CloudProgress.detail(.saving, file: entry.name))
271	                } catch {
272	                    // R6-20: a transcript refused after it was made, whose
273	                    // DELETE failed, is owed with no file to retry it from;
274	                    // everything below reads the refusal's own `ClientError`.
275	                    let refusal = error as? AssemblyAIClient.Refusal
276	                    if refusal?.deletion == .failed { report.refusedUndeleted.append(id) }
277	                    let error: any Error = refusal?.failure ?? error
278	                    if let client = error as? AssemblyAIClient.ClientError,
279	                        case .submissionUnresolved(let authenticationStatus) = client,
280	                        cancel.isCancelled || authenticationStatus != nil
281	                    {
282	                        throw client
283	                    }
284	                    if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
285	                    if let client = error as? AssemblyAIClient.ClientError {
286	                        if client == .cancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
287	                        // An auth failure ends the run at once: every later
288	                        // media would fail the same way and each costs an
289	                        // upload to find out.
290	                        if case .keyRefused = client { throw error }
291	                    }
292	                    if let native = error as? Transcriber.TranscribeError, native == .cancelled {
293	                        throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled
294	                    }
295	                    refuse(id, error.localizedDescription)
296	                }
297	            }
298	
299	            // (4) Every job on this media, derived from the one transcript.
300	            guard let file = files[id] else { continue }
301	            for job in grouped[id] ?? [] {
302	                let words = MediaTranscript.captionWords(for: job, in: file)
303	                    .filter { $0.start < job.start + job.duration }
304	                cues.append(
305	                    contentsOf: CaptionPages.cues(
306	                        from: words, span: job.span, frame: frame, request: pages,
307	                        engine: .assemblyai, clip: job.clip, media: job.media))
308	                if words.isEmpty {
309	                    problems.append(
310	                        CaptionLayout.Problem(
311	                            tag: "clip \(job.clip)", reason: "no speech was recognised in it"))
312	                } else {
313	                    clips.append(job.clip)
314	                }
315	            }
316	        }
317	
318	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
319	        guard !cues.isEmpty else {
320	            // `Transcriber.transcribe`'s two closing throws, same rule: "no
321	            // speech was recognised" is a claim about the AUDIO, and making
322	            // it when the audio was never read would send somebody looking
323	            // for words that are on the timeline.
324	            guard failures.isEmpty else {
325	                throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.failed(
326	                    failures.prefix(3).joined(separator: "; "))
327	            }
328	            throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.nothingRecognized
329	        }
330	        publish(1, "")
331	        return Transcriber.Outcome(cues: cues, problems: problems, clips: clips)
332	    }
333	}

336	/// The timeline transcript (road map "creator-jobs" TX1, spec §11 TX-10,
337	/// TX-13): every heard word of the edited container in timeline order,
338	/// nested instances included, each with its clip, track, editability and a
339	/// stable identity. Pure: it is handed the plan, the snapshot and each
340	/// media's source words, and reads no file, no cache and no window.
341	///
342	/// - `read` finds the INSTANCES — the plan's audio segments, each through
343	///   `Transcriber.jobs`' gate on its inner clip and the envelope's
344	///   `SilenceDetector.isAudible` — and the clips the gate refuses, found by
345	///   walking the clips rather than the segments (the core places no segment
346	///   for a clip with its audio off).
347	/// - `words` places each media's source words in each instance by R6-10's
348	///   mapping, orders them (start, end, front track first, source order),
349	///   counts their identities and asks `TimelineTranscript+Rules.swift`
350	///   whether each may be cut (TX-11).
351	/// - `window`, `overlapping`, `page` and `frameFloor` are TX-13's window and
352	///   paging.
353	enum TimelineTranscript {
354	
355	    /// A word's identity (TX-10): the enclosing nest clip ids, the media, the
356	    /// word's SOURCE start tick and k, the earlier words sharing the other
357	    /// three. The inner clip's id is left out: a ripple gives every split's
358	    /// second half a fresh id.
359	    struct Identity: Hashable {
360	        let nestPath: [UInt32]
361	        let media: UInt32
362	        let source: Ticks
363	        let k: Int
364	    }
365	
366	    /// One word of a media, in its SOURCE ticks. An on-device word's
367	    /// `source` is its MOVED start (TX-15); `recognisedStart` is the
368	    /// recogniser's own when TX-15 moved it.
369	    struct SourceWord: Equatable {
370	        let text: String
371	        let source: Ticks
372	        let sourceEnd: Ticks
373	        let speaker: String?
374	        var recognisedStart: Ticks? = nil
375	
376	        /// The tick an identity, a cut's match and a pause set key by
377	        /// (TX-17): the recogniser's start, moved or not.
378	        var identityTick: Ticks { recognisedStart ?? source }
379	    }
380	
381	    /// A heard media's words and where they came from.
382	    struct MediaWords: Equatable {
383	        let media: UInt32
384	        let engine: TranscriptionEngine
385	        let language: String?
386	        let fillersReported: Bool
387	        let words: [SourceWord]
388	        /// An on-device media read with no voice cache: its starts are the
389	        /// recogniser's, unmoved (TX-18).
390	        var voiceCacheMissing: Bool = false
391	    }
392	
393	    /// One heard instance: a plan audio segment, its inner clip, that clip's
394	    /// job (in its own container's time) and the CONTAINER track it plays
395	    /// under, with that track's stacking index.
396	    struct Instance: Equatable {
397	        let segment: PlanSegment
398	        let clip: ClipSnapshot
399	        let job: Transcriber.Job
400	        let track: UInt32
401	        let trackIndex: Int
402	    }
403	
404	    /// A media clip the gate refuses, and why.
405	    struct NoWords: Equatable {
406	        let clip: UInt32
407	        let nestPath: [UInt32]
408	        let tag: String
409	        let reason: String
410	    }
411	
412	    /// One word on the timeline.
413	    struct Word: Equatable {
414	        let text: String
415	        let start: Ticks
416	        let end: Ticks
417	        let clip: UInt32
418	        let track: UInt32
419	        let media: UInt32
420	        let engine: TranscriptionEngine
421	        let filler: Bool
422	        let speaker: String?
423	        let editable: Bool

429	    static let pageLimit = 2000

432	
433	    /// A cached media transcript's words: each word's start and
434	    /// `max(start, end)` through `MediaTranscript.sourceTicks`, the one door.
435	    static func sourceWords(cloud file: MediaTranscript.File) -> [SourceWord] {
436	        file.words.map {
437	            SourceWord(
438	                text: $0.text, source: MediaTranscript.sourceTicks(milliseconds: $0.start),
439	                sourceEnd: MediaTranscript.sourceTicks(milliseconds: max($0.start, $0.end)),
440	                speaker: $0.speaker)
441	        }
442	    }

444	    /// A stored on-device run's words, already media source ticks; with
445	    /// `moved` (`WordOnsets.moved`, one per word), each start moved to its
446	    /// sound and the recogniser's kept for its identity (TX-15, TX-17).
447	    static func sourceWords(
448	        device heard: DeviceTranscriptCache.Heard, moved: [Ticks]? = nil
449	    ) -> [SourceWord] {
450	        heard.words.enumerated().map { index, word in
451	            let end = max(word.start, word.end)
452	            guard let moved, index < moved.count, moved[index] != word.start else {
453	                return SourceWord(text: word.text, source: word.start, sourceEnd: end, speaker: nil)
454	            }
455	            return SourceWord(
456	                text: word.text, source: moved[index], sourceEnd: end, speaker: nil,
457	                recognisedStart: word.start)
458	        }
459	    }
